bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 起玄黓攝提格，盡昭陽赤奮若，凡十二年。

translations.literal: From Xuanji Shotige through Zhaoyang Chifenruo; twelve years in all.
translations.idiomatic: From Xuanji Shotige through Zhaoyang Chifenruo—twelve years in all.

sentences.zh: 1冬，上東擊韓王信餘寇於東垣，過柏人。

translations.literal: 1. In winter the sovereign went east to attack the remnant rebels of King Xin of Han at Dongyuan, passing Bo Ren.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In winter the Emperor marched east against the remnant rebels of King Xin of Han at Dongyuan, passing through Bo Ren.

sentences.zh: 貫高等壁人於廁中，欲以要上。

translations.literal: Guan Gao and others posted ambushers in the privy, intending to strike the sovereign there.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Gao and others posted assassins in the privy, intending to strike the Emperor there.

sentences.zh: 上欲宿，心動，問曰：「縣名為何？

translations.literal: The sovereign wished to lodge for the night; his heart stirred, and he asked: "What is this county called?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor meant to lodge for the night; his heart stirred, and he asked: "What is this county called?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「柏人。

translations.literal: " They replied: "Bo Ren.
translations.idiomatic: " They said, "Bo Ren."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「柏人者，迫於人也。

translations.literal: " The sovereign said: "'Bo Ren' means one forced upon others.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said, "'Bo Ren'—that is, one who forces himself upon others."

sentences.zh: 」遂不宿而去。

translations.literal: " He then did not lodge but departed.
translations.idiomatic: " He would not stay and went on.

sentences.zh: 十二月，帝行自東垣至。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the Emperor's procession returned from Dongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Emperor's procession returned from Dongyuan.

sentences.zh: ----2春，三月，行如洛陽。

translations.literal: ----2 In spring, the third month, he traveled to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In spring, the third month, he traveled to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: ----3令賈人毋得衣錦、繡、綺、縠、絺、紵、罽，操兵、乘、騎馬。

translations.literal: ----3 An order: merchants must not wear brocade, embroidery, damask, fine gauze, ramie, hemp, or felt; carry arms; ride in chariots; or ride horses.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 An edict forbade merchants to wear brocade, embroidery, damask, fine gauze, ramie, hemp, or felt, or to carry arms, ride in chariots, or ride horses.

sentences.zh: ----4秋，九月，行自洛陽至；

translations.literal: ----4 In autumn, the ninth month, his procession returned from Luoyang;
translations.idiomatic: ----4 In autumn, the ninth month, his procession returned from Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 淮南王、梁王、趙王、楚王皆從。

translations.literal: the kings of Huainan, Liang, Zhao, and Chu all followed.
translations.idiomatic: and the kings of Huainan, Liang, Zhao, and Chu all followed.

sentences.zh: ----5匈奴冒頓數苦北邊。

translations.literal: ----5 Modu of the Xiongnu repeatedly harried the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 Modu of the Xiongnu repeatedly harried the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 上患之，問劉敬，劉敬曰：「天下初定，士卒罷於兵，未可以武服也。

translations.literal: The sovereign was troubled by this and questioned Liu Jing; Liu Jing said: "All under Heaven is newly settled; the troops are weary of war—it cannot yet be subdued by force of arms.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was troubled and asked Liu Jing. Liu Jing said: "The realm is newly settled and the troops are weary of war—we cannot yet subdue them by force.

sentences.zh: 冒頓殺父代立，妻群母，以力為威，未可以仁義說也。

translations.literal: Modu killed his father and seized the throne in his place, took his father's consorts to wife, and makes might his awe—he cannot be persuaded by benevolence and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Modu killed his father and seized the throne, took his father's consorts to wife, and rules by force alone—he will not heed benevolence or righteousness.

sentences.zh: 獨可以計久遠，子孫為臣耳；

translations.literal: Only by a plan for the long term may his descendants become your subjects;
translations.idiomatic: Only a long-term design can make his descendants your subjects;

sentences.zh: 然恐陛下不能為。

translations.literal: yet I fear Your Majesty may not be able to do it.
translations.idiomatic: yet I fear Your Majesty may not be able to do it.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「奈何？

translations.literal: " The sovereign said: "What is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said, "What then?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「陛下誠能以適長公主妻之，厚奉遺之，彼必慕，以為閼氏，生子，必為太子。

translations.literal: " He replied: "If Your Majesty can truly give him the eldest princess by the proper wife in marriage, send her off with rich gifts, he will surely esteem her and make her khatun; when she bears a son, he will surely be made heir.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "If Your Majesty will give him the eldest princess by the proper wife, send her with rich gifts, he will surely esteem her and make her khatun; when she bears a son, that son will surely be heir.

sentences.zh: 陛下以歲時漢所餘，彼所鮮，數問遺，因使辨士風諭以禮節。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, with what Han has in surplus each season and what they lack, should repeatedly send gifts, and send eloquent persuaders to instruct them in ritual and propriety by example.
translations.idiomatic: Each season send what Han has in surplus and they lack, again and again; send eloquent persuaders to teach them ritual and propriety by example.

sentences.zh: 冒頓在，固為子婿；

translations.literal: While Modu lives, he will surely be your son-in-law;
translations.idiomatic: While Modu lives, he will be your son-in-law;

sentences.zh: 死，則外孫為單于；

translations.literal: when he dies, your grandson by a daughter will be chanyu;
translations.idiomatic: when he dies, your grandson will be chanyu;

sentences.zh: 豈嘗聞外孫敢與大父抗禮者哉！

translations.literal: who has ever heard of a grandson by a daughter daring to stand in rival ceremony with his mother's father!
translations.idiomatic: who has ever heard of a daughter's grandson daring to stand as equal to his mother's father!

sentences.zh: 可無戰以漸臣也。

translations.literal: You may make them subjects by degrees without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: You may make them subjects by degrees without fighting.

sentences.zh: 若陛下不能遣長公主，而令宗室及後宮詐稱公主，彼知，不肯貴近，無益也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty cannot send the eldest princess but orders kinsmen of the imperial clan and women of the inner palace to falsely call themselves princesses, when they know it they will not honor or draw near—and it will be of no use.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty cannot send the eldest princess but has clansmen and palace women falsely pose as princesses, once they know it they will not honor or draw near—and it will do no good.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「善！

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Excellent!
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said, "Excellent!"

sentences.zh: 」欲遣長公主。

translations.literal: " He wished to send the eldest princess.
translations.idiomatic: " He meant to send the eldest princess.

sentences.zh: 呂后日夜泣曰：「妾唯太子、一女，奈何棄之匈奴？

translations.literal: Empress Lü wept day and night, saying: "Your handmaid has only the heir and one daughter—how can we cast her away to the Xiongnu?
translations.idiomatic: Empress Lü wept day and night: "I have only the heir and one daughter—how can we cast her away to the Xiongnu?"

sentences.zh: 」上竟不能遣。

translations.literal: " The sovereign in the end could not send her.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor in the end could not send her.

sentences.zh: ----1冬，上取家人子名為長公主，以妻單于；

translations.literal: ----1 In winter the sovereign took a family member's daughter, styled her the eldest princess, and gave her to the chanyu in marriage;
translations.idiomatic: ----1 In winter the Emperor took a family member's daughter, styled her the eldest princess, and gave her to the chanyu in marriage;

sentences.zh: 使劉敬往結和親約。

translations.literal: he sent Liu Jing to conclude a treaty of harmonious kinship.
translations.idiomatic: and sent Liu Jing to conclude a treaty of harmonious kinship.

sentences.zh: ::臣光曰：建信侯謂冒頓殘賊，不可以仁義說，而欲與為婚姻，何前後之相違也！

translations.literal: :: Your servant Guang says: The Marquis of Jianxin said Modu is a cruel bandit who cannot be persuaded by benevolence and righteousness, yet wished to ally with him by marriage—how self-contradictory before and after!
translations.idiomatic: :: Your servant Guang says: The Marquis of Jianxin called Modu a cruel bandit who could not be moved by benevolence and righteousness, yet wished to ally with him by marriage—how his words contradict themselves!

sentences.zh: 夫骨肉之恩，尊卑之敘，唯仁義之人為能知之；

translations.literal: The affection between flesh and bone, the order of honor and baseness—only men of benevolence and righteousness can know them;
translations.idiomatic: The bonds of flesh and bone, the order of honor and baseness—only men of benevolence and righteousness can truly know them;

sentences.zh: 奈何欲以此服冒頓哉！

translations.literal: how then could you wish to subdue Modu by this!
translations.idiomatic: how then could you hope to subdue Modu by this!

sentences.zh: 蓋上世帝王之御夷狄也，服則懷之以德，叛則震之以威，未聞與為婚姻也。

translations.literal: The emperors and kings of high antiquity in governing the Yi and Di: if they submitted they cherished them with virtue; if they rebelled they awed them with might—one has not heard of making marriage alliances with them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors and kings of high antiquity governed the barbarians thus: if they submitted, they cherished them with virtue; if they rebelled, they awed them with might—one has never heard of marrying them.

sentences.zh: 且冒頓視其父如禽獸而獵之，奚有於婦翁！

translations.literal: Moreover, Modu regarded his father as a beast to be hunted—what regard would he have for a father-in-law!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Modu treated his father as a beast to be hunted—what regard would he have for a father-in-law!

sentences.zh: 建信侯之術，固已疏矣；

translations.literal: The Marquis of Jianxin's stratagem was already loose indeed;
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Jianxin's stratagem was already feeble;

sentences.zh: 況魯元已為趙后，又可奪乎！

translations.literal: how much more when Yuan of Lu was already queen of Zhao—could she be taken away!
translations.idiomatic: and when Yuan of Lu was already queen of Zhao, could she even be taken away!

sentences.zh: ----2劉敬從匈奴來，因言：「匈奴河南白羊、樓煩王，去長安近者七百里，輕騎一日一夜可以至秦中。

translations.literal: ----2 Liu Jing returned from the Xiongnu and therefore said: "The kings of the White Sheep and Loufan south of the Yellow River among the Xiongnu are, at their nearest, seven hundred li from Chang'an; light horsemen in one day and one night can reach the heart of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 Liu Jing returned from the Xiongnu and said: "The White Sheep and Loufan kings of the Xiongnu south of the Yellow River lie, at their nearest, seven hundred li from Chang'an; light horsemen can reach the heart of Qin in a day and a night.

sentences.zh: 秦中新破，少民，地肥饒，可益實。

translations.literal: The heart of Qin was newly broken and has few people; the land is rich and fertile—it can be filled and made solid.
translations.idiomatic: The heart of Qin was newly pacified and has few people, yet the land is rich and fertile—it can be filled and strengthened.

sentences.zh: 夫諸侯初起時，非齊諸田、楚昭、屈、景莫能興。

translations.literal: When the feudal lords first rose, none but the Tians of Qi and the Zhao, Qu, and Jing of Chu could stir.
translations.idiomatic: When the lords first rose, none but the Tians of Qi and the Zhao, Qu, and Jing of Chu could stir.

sentences.zh: 今陛下雖都關中，實少民，東有六國之強族，一日有變，陛下亦未得高枕而臥也。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty, though you have made your capital in the passes, in truth has few people; eastward are the powerful clans of the Six States—if one day there is trouble, Your Majesty also cannot lay your head on a high pillow and sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has made his capital in the passes, yet in truth has few people; eastward stand the powerful clans of the Six States—if trouble comes one day, Your Majesty cannot sleep on a high pillow either.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下徙六國後及豪桀、名家居關中，無事可以備胡，諸侯有變，亦足率以東伐。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty to move the descendants of the Six States and heroes, champions, and eminent families to dwell in the passes; when there is no affair they can guard against the Hu; if the feudal lords have trouble, they are also enough to lead eastward in attack.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant wishes Your Majesty to move the descendants of the Six States, heroes, champions, and eminent families to dwell in the passes; in peace they can guard against the Hu, and if the lords rebel, they are enough to lead an eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 此強本弱末之術也。

translations.literal: This is the method of strengthening the root and weakening the branches.
translations.idiomatic: This is the method of strengthening the root and weakening the branches.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「善！

translations.literal: " The sovereign said: "Excellent!
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said, "Excellent!"

sentences.zh: 」十一月，徙齊、楚大族昭氏、屈氏、景氏、懷氏、田氏五族及豪桀於關中，與利田、宅，凡十餘萬口。

translations.literal: " In the eleventh month he moved the great clans of Qi and Chu—the Zhao, Qu, Jing, Huai, and Tian families, five clans—and heroes and champions to the passes, granting them profitable fields and dwellings; in all more than a hundred thousand mouths.
translations.idiomatic: " In the eleventh month he moved the great clans of Qi and Chu—the Zhao, Qu, Jing, Huai, and Tian families, five clans—and heroes and champions to the passes, granting them profitable fields and dwellings—more than a hundred thousand people in all.

sentences.zh: ----3十二月，上行如洛陽。

translations.literal: ----3 In the twelfth month the sovereign traveled to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In the twelfth month the Emperor traveled to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: ----4貫高怨家知其謀，上變告之。

translations.literal: ----4 Guan Gao's enemies, learning of his plot, submitted a secret report.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 Guan Gao's enemies, learning of his plot, submitted a secret report.

sentences.zh: 於是上逮捕趙王及諸反者。

translations.literal: Thereupon the sovereign arrested the king of Zhao and all the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Emperor arrested the king of Zhao and all the rebels.

sentences.zh: 趙午等十餘人皆爭自剄，貫高獨怒罵曰：「誰令公為之？

translations.literal: Zhao Wu and more than ten others all strove to cut their own throats; Guan Gao alone raged and cursed, saying: "Who ordered you gentlemen to do this?
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wu and more than ten others all strove to cut their own throats; Guan Gao alone raged and cursed: "Who ordered you to do this?

sentences.zh: 今王實無謀，而並捕王。

translations.literal: Now the king in truth had no plot, yet you seize the king together with us.
translations.idiomatic: The king in truth had no plot, yet you seize the king together with us.

sentences.zh: 公等皆死，誰白王不反者？

translations.literal: When you gentlemen are all dead, who will declare for the king that he did not rebel?
translations.idiomatic: When you are all dead, who will declare to the world that the king did not rebel?

sentences.zh: 」乃轞車膠致，與王詣長安。

translations.literal: " He then had a barred cart made fast with glue and went with the king to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: " He then had a barred cart sealed with glue and went with the king to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 高對獄曰：「獨吾屬為之，王實不知。

translations.literal: Gao answered at trial: "Only our sort did it; the king in truth did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Gao answered at trial: "Only our sort did it; the king in truth did not know.

sentences.zh: 」吏治，搒笞數千，刺剟，身無可擊者，終不復言。

translations.literal: " The clerks prosecuted him; he was flogged with the stick thousands of times and stabbed and pierced until there was no place on his body left to strike—yet in the end he would not speak again.
translations.idiomatic: " The clerks prosecuted him; he was flogged thousands of times and stabbed and pierced until no inch of flesh remained to strike—yet he would not speak again.

sentences.zh: 呂后數言：「張王以公主故，不宜有此。

translations.literal: Empress Lü repeatedly said: "Because of the princess, King Zhang ought not suffer this.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Lü pleaded again and again: "For the princess's sake, King Zhang ought not suffer this."

sentences.zh: 」上怒曰：「使張敖據天下，豈少而女乎！

translations.literal: " The sovereign said in anger: "Had Zhang Ao possessed all under Heaven, would he have lacked your daughter!
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said in anger: "Had Zhang Ao possessed the realm, would he have lacked your daughter!"

sentences.zh: 」不聽。

translations.literal: " He would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " He would not listen.

sentences.zh: 廷尉以貫高事辭聞。

translations.literal: The commandant of justice reported Guan Gao's case and testimony to the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: The commandant of justice reported Guan Gao's case and testimony to the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「壯士！

translations.literal: The sovereign said: "A valiant man!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "A valiant man!

sentences.zh: 誰知者？

translations.literal: Who knows him?
translations.idiomatic: Who knows him?

sentences.zh: 以私問之。

translations.literal: Question him privately.
translations.idiomatic: Question him privately.

sentences.zh: 」中大夫洩公曰：「臣之邑子，素知之，此固趙國立義不侵，為然諾者也。

translations.literal: " Grandee Xie said: "A man of my native place—I have long known him. He is indeed one who stands on righteousness in Zhao and will not be violated, a man who keeps his word.
translations.idiomatic: " Grandee Xie said, "A man of my native place—I have long known him. He is one who stands on righteousness in Zhao and keeps his word."

sentences.zh: 」上使洩公持節往問之箯輿前。

translations.literal: " The sovereign sent Xie with credentials to question him before his bamboo litter.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor sent Xie with credentials to question him before his bamboo litter.

sentences.zh: 洩公與相勞苦，如生平歡，因問：「張王果有計謀不？

translations.literal: Xie exchanged greetings of hardship and toil with him as in former days' pleasure, and therefore asked: "Did King Zhang truly have a plot or not?
translations.idiomatic: Xie exchanged greetings with him as in former days' friendship, then asked: "Did King Zhang truly have a plot or not?"

sentences.zh: 」高曰：「人情寧不各愛其父母、妻子乎？

translations.literal: " Gao said: "Would human nature not have each man love his own parents and wife and children?
translations.idiomatic: " Gao said, "Would any man not love his own parents, wife, and children?

sentences.zh: 今吾三族皆以論死，豈愛王過於吾親哉？

translations.literal: Now my three clans are all condemned to death—how could I love the king more than my own kin?
translations.idiomatic: Now my three clans are all condemned to death—how could I love the king more than my own kin?

sentences.zh: 顧為王實不反，獨吾等為之。

translations.literal: Only that the king in truth did not rebel—it was we alone who did it.
translations.idiomatic: Only that the king in truth did not rebel—it was we alone who did it.

sentences.zh: 」具道本指所以為者、王不知狀。

translations.literal: " He fully set forth the original intent, why they had acted, and how the king did not know the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: " He fully set forth their original intent, why they had acted, and that the king did not know.

sentences.zh: 於是洩公入，具以報上。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xie entered and fully reported to the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Xie entered and fully reported to the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，上赦趙王敖，廢為宣平侯，徒代王如意為趙王。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the sovereign pardoned King Ao of Zhao, deposed him as Marquis of Xuanping, and moved the king of Dai, Ruyi, to be king of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, the Emperor pardoned King Ao of Zhao, reduced him to Marquis of Xuanping, and moved King Ruyi of Dai to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 上賢貫高為人，使洩公具告之曰：「張王已出。

translations.literal: The sovereign admired Guan Gao's character and had Xie fully tell him: "King Zhang has been released.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor admired Guan Gao's character and had Xie tell him in full: "King Zhang has been released."

sentences.zh: 」因赦貫高。

translations.literal: " He therefore pardoned Guan Gao.
translations.idiomatic: " He therefore pardoned Guan Gao.

sentences.zh: 貫高喜曰：「吾王審出乎？

translations.literal: Guan Gao said in joy: "Has my king truly been released?
translations.idiomatic: Guan Gao said joyfully, "Has my king truly been released?"

sentences.zh: 」洩公曰：「然。

translations.literal: " Xie said: "It is so.
translations.idiomatic: " Xie said, "It is so."

sentences.zh: 」洩公曰：「上多足下，故赦足下。

translations.literal: " Xie said: "The sovereign thinks much of you, and therefore pardoned you.
translations.idiomatic: " Xie said, "The Emperor thinks much of you, and therefore pardoned you."

sentences.zh: 」貫高曰：「所以不死，一身無餘者，白張王不反也。

translations.literal: " Gao said: "The reason I would not die though my body had nothing left was to declare that King Zhang did not rebel.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao said, "The reason I would not die though they left nothing of my body was to declare that King Zhang did not rebel.

sentences.zh: 今王已出，吾責已塞，死不恨矣。

translations.literal: Now the king has been released; my charge is fulfilled—to die is without regret.
translations.idiomatic: Now the king is released and my charge fulfilled—to die is without regret.

sentences.zh: 且人臣有篡弒之名，何面目復事上哉？

translations.literal: Moreover, a minister who bears the name of regicide—what face has he to serve the sovereign again?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, a minister who bears the name of regicide—what face has he to serve the Emperor again?

sentences.zh: 縱上不殺我，我不愧於心乎？

translations.literal: Even if the sovereign did not kill me, would I not be ashamed in my heart?
translations.idiomatic: Even if the Emperor did not kill me, would I not be ashamed in my own heart?

sentences.zh: 」乃仰絕亢，遂死。

translations.literal: " He then threw back his head and severed his throat, and died.
translations.idiomatic: " He threw back his head and cut his throat, and died.

sentences.zh: ::荀悅論曰：貫高首為亂謀，殺主之賊；

translations.literal: :: Xun Yue's discourse says: Guan Gao was first to plot rebellion—the assassin of his lord;
translations.idiomatic: :: Xun Yue writes: Guan Gao was first to plot rebellion—the assassin of his lord;

sentences.zh: 雖能證明其王，小亮不塞大逆，私行不贖公罪。

translations.literal: though he could prove his king innocent, a small brightness does not block a great rebellion; private conduct does not redeem public crime.
translations.idiomatic: though he could prove his king innocent, a small loyalty cannot offset a great crime; private conduct cannot redeem public guilt.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》之義大居正，罪無赦可也。

translations.literal: The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals is that the great must dwell in the correct—his crime admits no pardon.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals holds that the great must dwell in the correct—his crime admits no pardon.

sentences.zh: ::臣光曰：高祖驕以失臣，貫高狠以亡君。

translations.literal: :: Your servant Guang says: The High Ancestor through arrogance lost his ministers; Guan Gao through fierceness destroyed his lord.
translations.idiomatic: :: Your servant Guang says: The High Ancestor through arrogance lost his ministers; Guan Gao through fierceness destroyed his lord.

sentences.zh: 使貫高謀逆者，高祖之過也；

translations.literal: That Guan Gao plotted rebellion was the High Ancestor's fault;
translations.idiomatic: That Guan Gao plotted rebellion was the High Ancestor's fault;

translations.literal: that Zhang Ao lost his state was Guan Gao's crime.
translations.idiomatic: that Zhang Ao lost his kingdom was Guan Gao's crime.

translations.literal: ----5 An edict: "For crimes before bingyin, all from capital punishment downward are pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 An edict: "For crimes before bingyin, all from capital punishment downward are pardoned."

translations.idiomatic: " ----6 In the second month his procession returned from Luoyang.

translations.literal: ----7 At first the sovereign had decreed: "Among the ministers and retainers of Zhao, any who dared follow King Zhang—all their clans.
translations.idiomatic: ----7 At first the Emperor had decreed: "Among the ministers and retainers of Zhao, any who dared follow King Zhang—their clans shall be extinguished.

sentences.zh: 」郎中田叔、客孟舒皆處髡鉗為王家奴以從。

translations.literal: " The gentleman-of-the-palace Tian Shu and the retainer Meng Shu both submitted to shaving and fetters to become household slaves of the king and followed.
translations.idiomatic: " Gentleman-of-the-palace Tian Shu and retainer Meng Shu both submitted to shaving and fetters to become the king's household slaves and followed.

sentences.zh: 及張敖既免，上賢田叔、孟舒等。

translations.literal: When Zhang Ao was released, the sovereign admired Tian Shu, Meng Shu, and the others.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Ao was released, the Emperor admired Tian Shu, Meng Shu, and the others.

sentences.zh: 召見，與語，漢廷臣無能出其右者。

translations.idiomatic: He summoned them and spoke with them—none among the Han court ministers could surpass them.

sentences.zh: 上盡拜為郡守、諸侯相。

translations.literal: The sovereign appointed them all governors of commanderies and chancellors of feudal states.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor appointed them all governors of commanderies and chancellors of feudal states.

sentences.zh: ----8夏，六月，乙未晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: ----8 In summer, the sixth month, on the last day of the cycle yiwei, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: ----8 In summer, the sixth month, on the last day yiwei, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: ----9是歲，更以丞相何為相國。

translations.idiomatic: ----9 This year Chancellor He was made Chancellor of State.

translations.literal: 1. In summer, the fifth month, the Grand Imperial Father died at the Liyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In summer, the fifth month, the Grand Imperial Father died at the Liyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸卯，葬太上皇於萬年。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on guimao, the Grand Imperial Father was buried at Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on guimao, the Grand Imperial Father was buried at Wannian.

sentences.zh: 楚王、梁王皆來送葬。

translations.literal: The kings of Chu and Liang both came to attend the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: The kings of Chu and Liang both came to attend the funeral.

sentences.zh: 赦櫟陽囚。

translations.literal: Prisoners at Liyang were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners at Liyang were pardoned.

sentences.zh: ----2定陶戚姬有寵於上，生趙王如意。

translations.literal: ----2. Consort Qi of Dingtao had the sovereign's favor and bore the king of Zhao, Ruyi.
translations.idiomatic: ----2. Consort Qi of Dingtao had the Emperor's favor and bore the king of Zhao, Ruyi.

sentences.zh: 上以太子仁弱，謂如意類己；

translations.literal: The sovereign, considering the heir apparent benevolent and weak, said that Ruyi resembled himself;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, finding the heir apparent benevolent and weak, said that Ruyi resembled him;

sentences.zh: 雖封為趙王，常留之長安。

translations.literal: though enfeoffed as king of Zhao, he constantly kept him at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: though enfeoffed as king of Zhao, constantly kept him at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 上之關東，戚姬常從，日夜啼泣，欲立其子。

translations.literal: When the sovereign went east of the passes, Consort Qi often followed, weeping day and night, wishing to establish her son.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor went east of the passes, Consort Qi often followed, weeping day and night, wishing to make her son heir.

sentences.zh: 呂后年長，常留守，益疏。

translations.literal: Empress Lü was older and constantly remained to guard the capital, growing ever more estranged.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Lü was older and constantly remained to guard the capital, growing ever more estranged.

sentences.zh: 上欲廢太子而立趙王，大臣爭之，皆莫能得。

translations.literal: The sovereign wished to depose the heir apparent and establish the king of Zhao; the great ministers contended against it, yet none could prevail.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wished to depose the heir apparent and establish the king of Zhao; the great ministers contended against it, yet none could prevail.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫周昌廷爭之強，上問其說。

translations.literal: Grandee Secretary Zhou Chang contended strongly in court; the sovereign asked his reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: Grandee Secretary Zhou Chang contended strongly in court; the Emperor asked his reasoning.

sentences.zh: 昌為人吃，又盛怒，曰：「臣口不能言，然臣期期知其不可！

translations.literal: Chang was a man who stuttered, and was moreover in great anger. He said: "Your servant's mouth cannot speak, yet your servant ji-ji knows it cannot be done!
translations.idiomatic: Chang was a stutterer and was moreover in great anger. He said: "Your servant's mouth cannot speak, yet your servant ji-ji knows it cannot be done!

sentences.zh: 陛下欲廢太子，臣期期不奉詔！

translations.literal: If Your Majesty wishes to depose the heir apparent, your servant ji-ji will not obey the edict!
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty wishes to depose the heir apparent, your servant ji-ji will not obey the edict!

sentences.zh: 」上欣然而笑。

translations.literal: " The sovereign was pleased and laughed.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor was pleased and laughed.

sentences.zh: 呂后側耳於東廂聽，既罷，見昌，為跪謝，曰：「微君，太子幾廢！

translations.literal: Empress Lü listened with her ear at the side in the eastern wing. When it was over she saw Chang, knelt to thank him, and said: "Without you, sir, the heir apparent would nearly have been deposed!
translations.idiomatic: Empress Lü listened from the eastern wing. When it was over she saw Chang, knelt to thank him, and said: "Without you, sir, the heir apparent would nearly have been deposed!

sentences.zh: 時趙王年十歲，上憂萬歲之後不全也；

translations.literal: At that time the king of Zhao was ten years old; the sovereign worried that after ten thousand years he would not be kept whole;
translations.idiomatic: At that time the king of Zhao was ten years old; the Emperor worried that after his death Ruyi would not be kept safe;

sentences.zh: 符璽御史趙堯請為趙王置貴強相，及呂后、太子、群臣素所敬憚者。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk of Seals and Tallies Zhao Yao requested that for the king of Zhao there be set a noble and strong chancellor, and one whom the empress, the heir apparent, and the assembled ministers had always respected and feared.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk of Seals and Tallies Zhao Yao requested a noble and strong chancellor for the king of Zhao—one whom the empress, the heir apparent, and the assembled ministers had always respected and feared.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「誰可者？

translations.literal: The sovereign said: "Who will do?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Who will do?"

sentences.zh: 」堯曰：「御史大夫昌，其人也。

translations.literal: " Yao said: "Grandee Secretary Chang—that is the man.
translations.idiomatic: " Yao said: "Grandee Secretary Chang—that is the man."

sentences.zh: 」上乃以昌相趙，而以堯代昌為御史大夫。

translations.literal: " The sovereign thereupon made Chang chancellor of Zhao and replaced Chang with Yao as Grandee Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor thereupon made Chang chancellor of Zhao and replaced Chang with Yao as Grandee Secretary.

sentences.zh: ----3初，上以陽夏侯陳豨為相國，監趙、代邊兵；

translations.literal: ----3. Earlier, the sovereign had made Marquis of Yangxia Chen Xi chancellor of state, overseeing the border troops of Zhao and Dai;
translations.idiomatic: ----3. Earlier, the Emperor had made Marquis of Yangxia Chen Xi chancellor of state, overseeing the border troops of Zhao and Dai;

sentences.zh: 豨過辭淮陰侯。

translations.literal: Xi, passing by, took leave of the Marquis of Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, passing by, took leave of the Marquis of Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 淮陰侯挈其手，辟左右，與之步於庭，仰天歎曰：「子可與言乎？

translations.literal: The Marquis of Huaiyin took his hand, cleared away attendants, and walked with him in the courtyard, sighing to Heaven: "May I speak with you?
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Huaiyin took his hand, cleared away attendants, and walked with him in the courtyard, sighing to Heaven: "May I speak with you?"

sentences.zh: 」豨曰：「唯將軍令之！

translations.literal: " Xi said: "Only await the general's command!
translations.idiomatic: " Xi said: "Only await the general's command!"

sentences.zh: 」淮陰侯曰：「公之所居，天下精兵處也；

translations.literal: " The Marquis of Huaiyin said: "Where you dwell is where the elite troops of All under Heaven are;
translations.idiomatic: " The Marquis of Huaiyin said: "Where you dwell is where the elite troops of all under Heaven are;

sentences.zh: 而公，陛下之信幸臣也。

translations.literal: and you, sir, are a trusted and favored subject of Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: and you, sir, are a trusted and favored subject of Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 人言公之畔，陛下必不信；

translations.literal: If men say you have rebelled, Your Majesty will surely not believe it;
translations.idiomatic: If men say you have rebelled, Your Majesty will surely not believe it;

sentences.zh: 再至，陛下乃疑矣；

translations.literal: a second time, Your Majesty will then suspect;
translations.idiomatic: a second time, Your Majesty will then suspect;

sentences.zh: 三至，必怒而自將。

translations.literal: a third time, he will surely be angry and lead the army himself.
translations.idiomatic: a third time, he will surely be angry and lead the army himself.

sentences.zh: 吾為公從中起，天下可圖也。

translations.literal: I will rise for you from within; All under Heaven may be plotted for.
translations.idiomatic: I will rise for you from within; all under Heaven may be taken.

sentences.zh: 」陳豨素知其能也，信之，曰：「謹奉教！

translations.literal: " Chen Xi had always known his ability and trusted him, saying: "I respectfully receive your instruction!
translations.idiomatic: " Chen Xi had always known his ability and trusted him, saying: "I respectfully receive your instruction!"

sentences.zh: 豨常慕魏無忌之養士，及為相守邊，告歸，過趙，賓客隨之者千餘乘，邯鄲官舍皆滿。

translations.literal: Xi had always admired Lord Xinling of Wei's nurturing of knights. When he became chancellor and guarded the border, on requesting leave to return he passed through Zhao; retainers following him numbered more than a thousand chariots, and the official lodgings of Handan were all full.
translations.idiomatic: Xi had always admired Lord Xinling of Wei's nurturing of knights. When he became chancellor and guarded the border, on requesting leave to return he passed through Zhao; retainers following him numbered more than a thousand chariots, and the official lodgings of Handan were all full.

sentences.zh: 趙相周昌求入見上，具言豨賓客甚盛，擅兵於外數歲，恐有變。

translations.literal: Zhao's chancellor Zhou Chang sought to enter and see the sovereign, reporting fully that Xi's retainers were very numerous, that he had monopolized troops abroad for several years, and that there might be a change.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's chancellor Zhou Chang sought audience with the Emperor, reporting fully that Xi's retainers were very numerous, that he had held troops abroad for several years, and that there might be trouble.

sentences.zh: 上令人覆案豨客居代者諸不法事，多連引豨。

translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent men to re-investigate unlawful matters involving Xi's guests in Dai; many implicated Xi.

sentences.zh: 豨恐，韓王信因使王黃、曼丘臣等說誘之。

translations.literal: Xi was afraid; the king of Han Xin thereupon sent Wang Huang, Manqiu Chen, and others to persuade and entice him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was afraid; Han Xin the king of Han sent Wang Huang, Manqiu Chen, and others to persuade and entice him.

sentences.zh: 太上皇崩，上使人召豨，豨稱病不至；

translations.literal: The Grand Supreme Sovereign died; the sovereign sent men to summon Xi, but Xi claimed illness and did not come;
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Supreme Sovereign died; the Emperor sent men to summon Xi, but Xi claimed illness and did not come;

sentences.zh: 九月，遂與王黃等反，自立為代王，劫略趙、代。

translations.literal: in the ninth month he thereupon rebelled with Wang Huang and others, declared himself king of Dai, and plundered Zhao and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: in the ninth month he rebelled with Wang Huang and others, declared himself king of Dai, and plundered Zhao and Dai.

sentences.zh: 上自東擊之。

translations.literal: The sovereign himself went east to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor himself went east to attack him.

sentences.zh: 至邯鄲，喜曰：「豨不南據邯鄲而阻漳水，吾知其無能為矣。

translations.literal: Reaching Handan, he was pleased and said: "Xi did not seize Handan to the south and block the Zhang River—I know he can do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Handan, he was pleased and said: "Xi did not seize Handan to the south and block the Zhang River—I know he can do nothing."

sentences.zh: 周昌奏：「常山二十五城，亡其二十城；

translations.literal: Zhou Chang memorialized: "Of Changshan's twenty-five cities, twenty are lost;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chang memorialized: "Of Changshan's twenty-five cities, twenty are lost;

sentences.zh: 請誅守、尉。

translations.literal: I request that the governors and commandants be executed.
translations.idiomatic: I request that the governors and commandants be executed."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「守、尉反乎？

translations.literal: " The sovereign said: "Did the governors and commandants rebel?
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said: "Did the governors and commandants rebel?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「不。

translations.literal: " He replied: "No.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied: "No."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「是力不足，亡罪。

translations.literal: " The sovereign said: "Their strength was insufficient—no crime.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said: "Their strength was insufficient—no crime."

sentences.zh: 上令周昌選趙壯士可令將者，白見四人。

translations.literal: The sovereign ordered Zhou Chang to select stalwart men of Zhao fit to be made generals; he reported and presented four men.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Zhou Chang to select stalwart men of Zhao fit to be made generals; he presented four men.

sentences.zh: 上嫚罵曰：「豎子能為將乎？

translations.literal: The sovereign insulted and reviled them, saying: "Can striplings be generals?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor insulted and reviled them: "Can striplings be generals?"

sentences.zh: 」四人慚，皆伏地；

translations.literal: " The four were ashamed and all prostrated themselves;
translations.idiomatic: " The four were ashamed and all prostrated themselves;

sentences.zh: 上封各千戶，以為將。

translations.literal: the sovereign enfeoffed each with a thousand households and made them generals.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor enfeoffed each with a thousand households and made them generals.

sentences.zh: 左右諫曰；

translations.literal: Attendants at his side remonstrated, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Attendants at his side remonstrated:

sentences.zh: 「從入蜀、漢，伐楚，賞未遍行；

translations.literal: "From entering Shu and Han, attacking Chu, rewards have not yet been fully carried out;
translations.idiomatic: "From entering Shu and Han and attacking Chu, rewards have not yet been fully carried out;

sentences.zh: 今封此，何功？

translations.literal: now you enfeoff these—what merit?
translations.idiomatic: now you enfeoff these—what merit?"

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「非汝所知。

translations.literal: " The sovereign said: "This is not for you to know.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said: "This is not for you to know.

sentences.zh: 陳豨反，趙、代地皆豨有。

translations.literal: Chen Xi has rebelled; the lands of Zhao and Dai are all in Xi's possession.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xi has rebelled; the lands of Zhao and Dai are all in Xi's possession.

sentences.zh: 吾以羽檄征天下兵，未有至者，今計唯獨邯鄲中兵耳。

translations.literal: I have summoned the troops of All under Heaven with urgent dispatch, yet none have arrived; at present the plan relies only on the troops within Handan.
translations.idiomatic: I have summoned the troops of all under Heaven with urgent dispatch, yet none have arrived; at present the plan relies only on the troops within Handan.

sentences.zh: 吾何愛四千戶，不以慰趙子弟！

translations.literal: Why should I begrudge four thousand households and not use them to comfort the youths of Zhao!
translations.idiomatic: Why should I begrudge four thousand households and not use them to comfort the youths of Zhao!"

sentences.zh: 」皆曰：「善！

translations.literal: " All said: "Excellent!
translations.idiomatic: " All said: "Excellent!"

sentences.zh: 又聞豨將皆故賈人，上曰：「吾知所以與之矣。

translations.literal: He also heard that Xi's generals were all former merchants. The sovereign said: "I know how to deal with them.
translations.idiomatic: He also heard that Xi's generals were all former merchants. The Emperor said: "I know how to deal with them."

sentences.zh: 」乃多以金購豨將，豨將多降。

translations.literal: " He thereupon used much gold to buy over Xi's generals; many of Xi's generals surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon used much gold to buy over Xi's generals; many of Xi's generals surrendered.

sentences.zh: ----1冬，上在邯鄲。

translations.literal: ----1. In winter the sovereign was at Handan.
translations.idiomatic: ----1. In winter the Emperor was at Handan.

sentences.zh: 陳豨將侯敞將萬餘人遊行，王黃將騎千餘軍曲逆，張春將卒萬餘人渡河攻聊城。

translations.literal: Chen Xi's general Hou Chang led more than ten thousand men on the march; Wang Huang led more than a thousand horsemen and encamped at Quyi; Zhang Chun led more than ten thousand soldiers across the river to attack Liaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xi's general Hou Chang led more than ten thousand men on the march; Wang Huang led more than a thousand horsemen and encamped at Quyi; Zhang Chun led more than ten thousand soldiers across the river to attack Liaocheng.

sentences.zh: 漢將軍郭蒙與齊將擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Han general Guo Meng joined with a Qi general to attack and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Han general Guo Meng joined with a Qi general to attack and inflicted a great defeat.

sentences.zh: 太尉周勃道太原入定代地，至馬邑，不下，攻殘之。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Zhou Bo went by way of Taiyuan to settle Dai; reaching Mayi, it would not submit, so he attacked and ravaged it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Zhou Bo went by way of Taiyuan to settle Dai; reaching Mayi, it would not submit, so he attacked and ravaged it.

sentences.zh: 趙利守東垣，帝攻拔之，更命曰真定。

translations.literal: Zhao Li held Dongyuan; the Emperor attacked and took it and renamed it Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Li held Dongyuan; the Emperor attacked and took it and renamed it Zhending.

sentences.zh: 帝購王黃、曼丘臣以千金，其麾下皆生致之。

translations.literal: The Emperor offered a thousand in gold for Wang Huang and Manqiu Chen; their subordinates were all captured alive and delivered.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor offered a thousand in gold for Wang Huang and Manqiu Chen; their subordinates were all captured alive and delivered.

sentences.zh: 於是陳豨軍遂敗。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chen Xi's army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Chen Xi's army was defeated.

sentences.zh: 淮陰侯信稱病，不從擊豨，陰使人至豨所，與通謀。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Huaiyin Xin claimed illness and did not follow in attacking Xi, but secretly sent men to Xi's place to communicate in conspiracy.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Huaiyin Xin claimed illness and did not follow in attacking Xi, but secretly sent men to Xi's camp to conspire with him.

sentences.zh: 信謀與家臣夜詐詔赦諸官徒、奴，欲發以襲呂后、太子；

translations.literal: Xin plotted with household retainers by night to forge an edict pardoning all convict laborers and slaves, intending to raise them to strike Empress Lü and the heir apparent;
translations.idiomatic: Xin plotted with household retainers by night to forge an edict pardoning all convict laborers and slaves, intending to raise them to strike Empress Lü and the heir apparent;

sentences.zh: 部署已定，待豨報。

translations.literal: the deployment was already settled, awaiting Xi's report.
translations.idiomatic: the deployment was already settled, awaiting Xi's report.

sentences.zh: 其舍人得罪於信，信囚，欲殺之。

translations.literal: A house steward had offended Xin; Xin imprisoned him and wished to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: A house steward had offended Xin; Xin imprisoned him and wished to kill him.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，舍人弟上變，告信欲反狀於呂后。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the steward's younger brother reported the emergency, informing Empress Lü of Xin's intended rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, the steward's younger brother reported the emergency, informing Empress Lü of Xin's intended rebellion.

sentences.zh: 呂后欲召，恐其儻不就，乃與蕭相國謀，詐令人從上所來，言豨已得，死，列侯、群臣皆賀。

translations.literal: Empress Lü wished to summon him but feared that perhaps he would not come; she therefore plotted with Chancellor Xiao, falsely sending a man from where the sovereign was, saying that Xi had been taken and was dead, and that marquises and assembled ministers all congratulated.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Lü wished to summon him but feared he might not come; she plotted with Chancellor Xiao, falsely sending a man from the Emperor's camp saying that Xi had been taken and was dead, and that marquises and assembled ministers all congratulated.

sentences.zh: 相國紿信曰：「雖疾，強入賀。

translations.literal: The chancellor deceived Xin, saying: "Though ill, force yourself to enter and congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor deceived Xin: "Though ill, force yourself to enter and congratulate."

sentences.zh: 」信入，呂后使武士縛信，斬之長樂鐘室。

translations.literal: " Xin entered; Empress Lü had warriors bind Xin and behead him in the Bell Room of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: " Xin entered; Empress Lü had warriors bind Xin and behead him in the Bell Room of Changle.

sentences.zh: 信方斬，曰：「吾悔不用蒯徹之計，乃為兒女子所詐，豈非天哉？

translations.literal: As Xin was about to be beheaded he said: "I regret not using Kuai Che's plan—to be deceived by women and children, is this not Heaven's doing?
translations.idiomatic: As Xin was about to be beheaded he said: "I regret not using Kuai Che's plan—to be deceived by women and children, is this not Heaven's doing?"

sentences.zh: 」遂夷信三族。

translations.literal: " He thereupon exterminated Xin's three clans.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon exterminated Xin's three clans.

sentences.zh: ::臣光曰：世或以韓信為首建大策，與高祖起漢中，定三秦，遂分兵以北，禽魏，取代，僕趙，脅燕，東擊齊而有之，南滅楚垓下，漢之所以得天下者，大抵皆信之功也。

translations.literal: :: Your servant Guang says: The age sometimes takes Han Xin as the first to frame the great design, rising with the High Ancestor from Hanzhong, settling the Three Qins, then dividing troops northward—capturing Wei, taking Dai, subduing Zhao, coercing Yan, striking east to take Qi, and south destroying Chu at Gaixia. That Han won All under Heaven was, broadly speaking, mostly Xin's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: :: Your servant Guang says: The age sometimes takes Han Xin as the first to frame the great design, rising with the High Ancestor from Hanzhong, settling the Three Qins, then dividing troops northward—capturing Wei, taking Dai, subduing Zhao, coercing Yan, striking east to take Qi, and south destroying Chu at Gaixia. That Han won all under Heaven was, broadly speaking, mostly Xin's achievement.

sentences.zh: 觀其距蒯徹之說，迎高祖於陳，豈有反心哉？

translations.literal: Observing how he rejected Kuai Che's counsel yet received the High Ancestor at Chen—how could he have had a rebellious heart?
translations.idiomatic: Observing how he rejected Kuai Che's counsel yet received the High Ancestor at Chen—how could he have had a rebellious heart?

sentences.zh: 良由失職怏怏，遂陷悖逆。

translations.literal: It was truly because, losing his post, he was resentful and discontented, and so fell into rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: It was truly because, losing his post, he was resentful and discontented, and so fell into rebellion.

sentences.zh: 夫以盧綰里閈舊恩，猶南面王燕，信乃以列侯奉朝請，豈非高祖亦有負於信哉？

translations.literal: That Lu Wan, through old neighborhood kindness, still faced south as king of Yan, while Xin merely as a ranked marquis attended court—is this not that the High Ancestor too had wronged Xin?
translations.idiomatic: That Lu Wan, through old neighborhood ties, still faced south as king of Yan, while Xin merely as a ranked marquis attended court—is this not that the High Ancestor too had wronged Xin?

sentences.zh: 臣以為高祖用詐謀禽信於陳，言負則有之；

translations.literal: Your servant considers that the High Ancestor used deceitful stratagems to capture Xin at Chen—to speak of wronging him is so;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant considers that the High Ancestor used deceitful stratagems to capture Xin at Chen—to speak of wronging him is so;

sentences.zh: 雖然，信亦有以取之也。

translations.literal: even so, Xin too had grounds on which he brought it upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: even so, Xin too had grounds on which he brought it upon himself.

sentences.zh: 始，漢與楚相距滎陽，信滅齊，不還報而自王；

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Han and Chu faced each other at Yingyang, Xin destroyed Qi, did not return to report, and made himself king;
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning, when Han and Chu faced each other at Yingyang, Xin destroyed Qi, did not return to report, and made himself king;

sentences.zh: 其後漢追楚至固陵，與信期共攻楚而信不至。

translations.literal: afterward Han pursued Chu to Guling and fixed a date with Xin to attack Chu together, yet Xin did not come.
translations.idiomatic: afterward Han pursued Chu to Guling and fixed a date with Xin to attack Chu together, yet Xin did not come.

sentences.zh: 當是之時，高祖固有取信之心矣，顧力不能耳。

translations.literal: At that time the High Ancestor already had a mind to take Xin in, only his strength was insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the High Ancestor already had a mind to take Xin in, only his strength was insufficient.

sentences.zh: 及天下已定，則信復何恃哉？

translations.literal: When All under Heaven was already settled, what could Xin again rely upon?
translations.idiomatic: When all under Heaven was already settled, what could Xin again rely upon?

sentences.zh: 夫乘時以徼利者，市井之志也；

translations.literal: To seize the moment and seek profit is the ambition of the marketplace;
translations.idiomatic: To seize the moment and seek profit is the ambition of the marketplace;

sentences.zh: 酬功而報德者，士君子之心也。

translations.literal: to repay merit and return kindness is the heart of the gentleman and scholar.
translations.idiomatic: to repay merit and return kindness is the heart of the gentleman and scholar.

sentences.zh: 信以市井之志利其身，而以君子之心望於人，不亦難哉？

translations.literal: Xin used the marketplace ambition to profit himself, yet with the gentleman's heart expected it of others—is this not difficult?
translations.idiomatic: Xin used the marketplace ambition to profit himself, yet with the gentleman's heart expected it of others—is this not difficult?

sentences.zh: 是故太史公論之曰：「假令韓信學道謙讓，不伐己功，不矜其能，則庶幾哉？

translations.literal: Therefore the Grand Historian judged, saying: "Suppose Han Xin had studied the Way, been modest and yielding, not boasted of his own merit, not prided himself on his ability—then might he not have fared thus?
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Grand Historian judged: "Suppose Han Xin had studied the Way, been modest and yielding, not boasted of his own merit, not prided himself on his ability—then might he not have fared thus?

sentences.zh: 於漢家勳，可以比周、召、太公之徒，後世血食矣！

translations.literal: Among Han's meritorious servants he could have been compared to the Duke of Zhou, the Duke of Shao, and Grand Duke Jiang, and later ages would have offered blood sacrifice!
translations.idiomatic: Among Han's meritorious servants he could have been compared to the Duke of Zhou, the Duke of Shao, and Grand Duke Jiang, and later ages would have offered blood sacrifice!

sentences.zh: 不務出此，而天下已集，乃謀畔逆；

translations.literal: Not pursuing this course, yet when All under Heaven was already gathered he plotted rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: Not pursuing this course, yet when all under Heaven was already gathered he plotted rebellion;

sentences.zh: 夷滅宗族，不亦宜乎？

translations.literal: to exterminate his clan—was it not fitting?
translations.idiomatic: to exterminate his clan—was it not fitting?"

translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon edicted Qi to arrest Kuai Che.

translations.idiomatic: " Che said: "Alas!

translations.idiomatic: To be boiled is a grievous wrong!

translations.literal: " The sovereign said: "You taught Han Xin to rebel—what wronged suffering is this?
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said: "You taught Han Xin to rebel—what wrong is there in boiling you?

translations.idiomatic: Zhi's dog barked at Yao—Yao was not unkind; dogs naturally bark at anyone who is not their master.

sentences.zh: 當是時，臣唯獨知韓信，非知陛下也。

translations.literal: At that time your servant knew only Han Xin, not Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: At that time I knew only Han Xin, not Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 且天下銳精持鋒欲為陛下所為者甚眾，顧力不能耳，又可盡烹之邪？

translations.literal: Moreover, those under Heaven who sharpen their essence and hold their blades wishing to do what Your Majesty has done are many—only that their strength cannot; could you boil them all?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, countless men under Heaven sharpen their wits and grip their blades wishing to do what Your Majesty has done—only that their strength fails; could you boil them all?

translations.idiomatic: ----6 When the Emperor campaigned against Chen Xi, he called up troops from Liang;

translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was angry and sent a man to rebuke him.

translations.idiomatic: The King of Liang was afraid and wished to go in person to apologize.

translations.idiomatic: His general Hu Zhe said: "Your Majesty at first did not go; now, rebuked, if you go you will be seized.

translations.idiomatic: Better to raise troops and rebel at once.

translations.literal: " The King of Liang did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " The King of Liang did not listen.

translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Emperor sent envoys to seize the King of Liang; he did not perceive it and was imprisoned at Luoyang.

translations.literal: The relevant officials prosecuted that "the marks of rebellion are complete; we request judgment according to law"; the sovereign pardoned him and made him a commoner, sending him under escort to Qingyi in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant officials prosecuted that "the marks of rebellion are complete; we request judgment according to law"; the Emperor pardoned him and made him a commoner, sending him under escort to Qingyi in Shu.

sentences.zh: 西至鄭，逢呂后從長安來。

translations.literal: Going west he reached Zheng and met the Empress Lü coming from Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Going west he reached Zheng and met Empress Lü coming from Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 彭王為呂后泣涕，自言無罪，願處故昌邑。

translations.literal: The King of Peng wept for the Empress Lü and said himself guiltless, wishing to dwell at his former Changyi.
translations.idiomatic: King Peng wept before Empress Lü, declared himself guiltless, and asked to remain at his former seat of Changyi.

translations.idiomatic: Empress Lü promised and traveled east with him.

translations.idiomatic: Reaching Luoyang, Empress Lü told the Emperor: "King Peng is a stalwart man; exiling him to Shu now is to leave trouble for yourself;

translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Wang Tian Guan memorialized requesting extinction of his clan; the Emperor approved the memorial.

translations.literal: In the third month, the house of Yue was extinguished to the third degree.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Peng Yue's clan was extinguished to the third degree.

translations.idiomatic: Peng Yue's head was displayed at Luoyang; an edict: "Whoever collects and views it shall be arrested at once.

translations.idiomatic: Luan Bu, a great officer of Liang, had been envoy to Qi; on his return he reported his business beneath Peng Yue's head, sacrificed, and wept for him.

sentences.zh: 吏捕以聞。

translations.idiomatic: Officers arrested him and reported it.

translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned Bu, reviled him, and wished to boil him alive.

sentences.zh: 方提趨湯，布顧曰：「願一言而死。

translations.literal: Just as they were dragging him toward the cauldron, Bu looked back, saying: "I wish one word before I die.
translations.idiomatic: Just as they were dragging him toward the cauldron, Bu looked back and said: "Let me speak one word before I die.

translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said: "What word?"
