sentences.zh: 」即被佗書，行南海尉事。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he invested Tuo with the writ and charged him with the affairs of Nanhai Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he invested Tuo with the writ and charged him with the affairs of Commandant of Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 囂死，佗即移檄告橫浦、陽山、湟谿關曰：「盜兵且至，急絕道，聚兵自守！

translations.literal: Xiao died; Tuo at once issued a proclamation to the passes of Hengpu, Yangshan, and Huangxi, saying: "Bandit troops are about to arrive—hasten to cut the roads, gather troops, and defend yourselves!
translations.idiomatic: Xiao died; Tuo at once issued a proclamation to the passes of Hengpu, Yangshan, and Huangxi: "Bandit troops are about to arrive—hasten to cut the roads, gather troops, and defend yourselves!

sentences.zh: 」因稍以法誅秦所置長吏，以其黨為假守。

translations.literal: " Then gradually by law he executed the long-term officials Qin had placed, making his faction acting administrators.
translations.idiomatic: " Then gradually, by law, he executed the senior officials Qin had placed and made his own followers acting administrators.

sentences.zh: 秦已破滅，佗即擊並桂林、象郡，自立為南越武王。

translations.literal: Qin was already broken and extinguished; Tuo at once attacked and annexed Guilin and Xiang commanderies and established himself as Martial King of Nanyue.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin was broken and extinguished, Tuo attacked and annexed Guilin and Xiang commanderies and made himself Martial King of Nanyue.

sentences.zh: 陸生至，尉佗魋結、箕倨見陸生。

translations.literal: Master Lu arrived; Wei Tuo wore his hair in a chignon and sat with legs spread insolently to receive Master Lu.
translations.idiomatic: When Master Lu arrived, Zhao Tuo wore his hair in a chignon and received him sitting with legs spread insolently.

sentences.zh: 陸生說佗曰：「足下中國人，親戚、昆弟墳墓在真定。

translations.literal: Master Lu urged Tuo: "Your feet are a man of the Central States; your kinsmen and the graves of brothers are at Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Master Lu urged him: "You are a man of the Central States; your kinsmen and your brothers' graves are at Zhending.

sentences.zh: 今足下反天性，棄冠帶，欲以區區之越與天子抗衡為敵國，禍且及身矣。

translations.literal: Now your feet turn against Heaven-nature, cast off cap and sash, and wish with the mere Yue to oppose the Son of Heaven as enemy state—disaster will reach your person.
translations.idiomatic: Now you turn against your nature, cast off cap and sash, and wish with mere Yue to oppose the Son of Heaven as an enemy state—disaster will reach you.

sentences.zh: 且夫秦失其政，諸族、豪桀並起，唯漢王先入關，據咸陽。

translations.literal: Moreover Qin lost its government; all clans and powerful heroes rose together, yet only the King of Han entered the passes first and held Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Qin lost its government; clans and powerful heroes rose everywhere, yet only the King of Han entered the passes first and held Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 項羽倍約，自立為西楚霸王，諸侯皆屬，可謂至強。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu broke faith, made himself Western Chu Overlord, and all feudal lords submitted—one may say supremely strong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu broke faith, made himself Western Chu Overlord, and all feudal lords submitted—he was supremely strong.

sentences.zh: 然漢王起巴、蜀，鞭笞天下，遂誅項羽，滅之。

translations.literal: Yet the King of Han rose from Ba and Shu, whipped all under Heaven, and in the end executed Xiang Yu and extinguished him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the King of Han rose from Ba and Shu, whipped the realm, and in the end executed Xiang Yu and destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 五年之間，海內平定。

translations.literal: Within five years the realm within the seas was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Within five years the realm was pacified.

sentences.zh: 此非人力，天之所建也。

translations.literal: This is not human strength—it is what Heaven has established.
translations.idiomatic: This is not human strength—it is what Heaven has established.

sentences.zh: 天子聞君王王南越，不助天下誅暴逆，將相欲移兵而誅王。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven heard that you, king, ruled Southern Yue and did not aid all under Heaven in punishing violent rebels; ministers and generals wished to move troops to execute you.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven heard that you ruled Southern Yue and did not aid the realm in punishing violent rebels; ministers and generals wished to move troops to execute you.

sentences.zh: 天子憐百姓新勞苦，故且休之，遣臣授君王印，剖符通使。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven pitied the people newly wearied and toiled, so for the time rested them and sent your servant to invest you with the king's seal and split tally for mutual envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven pitied the people, newly wearied and toiled, so for now he rested them and sent me to invest you with the king's seal and split tally for mutual envoys.

sentences.zh: 君王宜郊迎，北面稱臣；

translations.literal: You, king, ought to meet him in the suburbs and face north as subject;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty ought to meet him in the suburbs and face north as subject;

sentences.zh: 乃欲以新造未集之越，屈強於此！

translations.literal: yet you wish with newly made, not yet gathered Yue to bend strength here!
translations.idiomatic: yet you wish with newly made, not yet gathered Yue to stand defiant here!

sentences.zh: 漢誠聞之，掘燒王先人塚，夷滅宗族，使一偏將將十萬眾臨越，則越殺王降漢如反覆手耳。

translations.literal: If Han truly heard of it, they would dig up and burn your king's forefathers' graves, extinguish clan and kindred, and send one wing general with a host of a hundred thousand to descend on Yue—then Yue would kill its king and surrender to Han like turning the hand.
translations.idiomatic: If Han truly heard of it, they would dig up and burn your forefathers' graves, extinguish your clan, and send one wing general with a host of a hundred thousand against Yue—then Yue would kill its king and surrender to Han like turning the hand.

sentences.zh: 」於是尉佗乃蹶然起坐，謝陸生曰：「居蠻夷中久，殊失禮義。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Wei Tuo suddenly started up and sat, apologizing to Master Lu: "Dwelling long among barbarian Yi, I have utterly lost rites and propriety.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Zhao Tuo suddenly rose and sat, apologizing to Master Lu: "Dwelling long among barbarians, I have utterly lost rites and propriety.

sentences.zh: 」因問陸生曰：「我孰與蕭何、曹參、韓信賢？

translations.literal: " Then he asked Master Lu: "Compared with Xiao He, Cao Shen, and Han Xin—which am I the more worthy?"
translations.idiomatic: " Then he asked Master Lu: "Compared with Xiao He, Cao Shen, and Han Xin—which of us is the worthier?"

sentences.zh: 」陸生曰：「王似賢也。

translations.literal: " Master Lu said: "Your Majesty seems worthy."
translations.idiomatic: " Master Lu said: "Your Majesty seems worthy."

sentences.zh: 」復曰：「我孰與皇帝賢？

translations.literal: " Again he said: "Compared with the Emperor—which am I the more worthy?"
translations.idiomatic: " Again he asked: "Compared with the Emperor—which of us is the worthier?"

sentences.zh: 」陸生曰：「皇帝繼五帝、三皇之業，統理中國；

translations.literal: " Master Lu said: "The Emperor continues the enterprise of the Five Emperors and Three August Ones, governing and ordering the Central States;
translations.idiomatic: " Master Lu said: "The Emperor continues the enterprise of the Five Emperors and Three August Ones and governs the Central States;

sentences.zh: 中國之人以億計，地方萬里，萬物殷富；

translations.literal: the people of the Central States number in the hundreds of millions; territory ten thousand li; all things abundant and rich;
translations.idiomatic: its people number in the hundreds of millions; its territory spans ten thousand li; all things are abundant and rich;

sentences.zh: 政由一家，自天地剖判未始有也。

translations.literal: government from one house—from when Heaven and Earth were first split there has never been such.
translations.idiomatic: government from one house—from when Heaven and Earth were first split there has never been such.

sentences.zh: 今王眾不過十萬，皆蠻夷，崎嶇山海間，譬若漢一郡耳，何乃比於漢？

translations.literal: Now your Majesty's masses are no more than a hundred thousand, all barbarian Yi in rugged mountains and seas—comparable to but one commandery of Han; how then compare with Han?"
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty's masses are no more than a hundred thousand, all barbarians in rugged mountains and seas—comparable to but one commandery of Han; how then compare with Han?"

sentences.zh: 」尉佗大笑曰：「吾不起中國，故王此；

translations.literal: " Wei Tuo laughed greatly: "I did not rise in the Central States, therefore I am king here;
translations.idiomatic: " Zhao Tuo laughed loudly: "I did not rise in the Central States, therefore I am king here;

sentences.zh: 使我居中國，何遽不若漢？

translations.literal: had you placed me in the Central States, how would I suddenly fail to match Han?"
translations.idiomatic: had you placed me in the Central States, how would I suddenly fail to match Han?"

sentences.zh: 」乃留陸生與飲。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he detained Master Lu to drink with him.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he detained Master Lu to drink with him.

sentences.zh: 數月，曰：「越中無足與語。

translations.literal: After several months he said: "Within Yue there is no one fit to speak with.
translations.idiomatic: After several months he said: "Within Yue there is no one fit to speak with.

sentences.zh: 至生來，令我日聞所不聞。

translations.literal: When the Gentleman came, he made me day by day hear what I had not heard."
translations.idiomatic: When the Gentleman came, he made me day by day hear what I had never heard."

sentences.zh: 」賜陸生橐中裝直千金，他送亦千金。

translations.literal: " He bestowed on Master Lu goods in the sack worth a thousand in gold, and other gifts also a thousand in gold.
translations.idiomatic: " He bestowed on Master Lu goods in his sack worth a thousand in gold, and other gifts also worth a thousand in gold.

sentences.zh: 陸生卒拜尉佗為南越王，令稱臣，奉漢約。

translations.literal: Master Lu in the end enfeoffed Wei Tuo as King of Nanyue, ordering him to call himself subject and observe Han's covenant.
translations.idiomatic: Master Lu in the end enfeoffed Zhao Tuo as King of Nanyue, ordering him to call himself subject and observe Han's covenant.

sentences.zh: 歸報，帝大悅，拜賈為太中大夫。

translations.literal: Returning to report, the Emperor was greatly pleased and appointed Jia Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he reported; the Emperor was greatly pleased and appointed Jia Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 陸生時時前說稱《詩》、《書》，帝罵之曰：「乃公居馬上而得之，安事《詩》、《書》？

translations.literal: Master Lu from time to time advanced and urged, praising the Odes and Documents; the Emperor reviled him: "Your daddy got it on horseback—what business have the Odes and Documents?
translations.idiomatic: Master Lu from time to time advanced and praised the Odes and Documents; the Emperor reviled him: "Your daddy got it on horseback—what business have the Odes and Documents?

sentences.zh: 」陸生曰：「居馬上得之，寧可以馬上治之乎？

translations.literal: " Master Lu said: "Got it on horseback—can you govern it on horseback?
translations.idiomatic: " Master Lu said: "You got it on horseback—can you govern it on horseback?

sentences.zh: 且湯、武逆取而以順守之；

translations.literal: Moreover Tang and Wu took it in reversal but guarded it in accordance;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Tang and Wu took it by force but guarded it by compliance;

sentences.zh: 文武並用，長久之術也。

translations.literal: civil and martial employed together—that is the art of long endurance.
translations.idiomatic: civil and martial employed together—that is the art of long endurance.

sentences.zh: 昔者吳王夫差、智伯、秦始皇，皆以極武而亡。

translations.literal: In the past King Fuchai of Wu, Earl Zhi, and the First Emperor of Qin all by extreme martialism perished.
translations.idiomatic: In the past King Fuchai of Wu, Earl Zhi, and the First Emperor of Qin all perished through extreme martialism.

sentences.zh: 鄉使秦已並天下，行仁義，法先聖，陛下安得而有之？

translations.literal: If only Qin had already united all under Heaven and practiced benevolence and righteousness, taking the former sages as model, how would Your Majesty have obtained it?"
translations.idiomatic: If Qin had already united the realm and practiced benevolence and righteousness, taking the former sages as model, how would Your Majesty have obtained it?"

sentences.zh: 」帝有慚色，曰：「試為我著秦所以失天下、吾所以得之者及古成敗之國。

translations.literal: " The Emperor had a look of shame and said: "Try to write for me how Qin lost all under Heaven, how We obtained it, and states of antiquity whose success and failure...
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor looked ashamed and said: "Try to write for me how Qin lost the realm, how I obtained it, and the success and failure of states in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 」陸生乃粗述存亡之征，凡著十二篇。

translations.literal: " Master Lu then roughly set forth the signs of survival and perdition, all together composing twelve chapters.
translations.idiomatic: " Master Lu then roughly set forth the signs of survival and perdition, composing twelve chapters in all.

sentences.zh: 每奏一篇，帝未嘗不稱善，左右呼萬歲；

translations.literal: Each time he presented a chapter, the Emperor never failed to praise it well, and those at his sides cried "ten thousand years";
translations.idiomatic: Each time he presented a chapter, the Emperor never failed to praise it, and those at his sides cried "ten thousand years";

sentences.zh: 號其書曰《新語》。

translations.literal: they styled his book New Discourses.
translations.idiomatic: they styled his book New Discourses.

sentences.zh: ----10帝有疾，惡見人，臥禁中，詔戶者無得入群臣，群臣絳、灌等莫敢入，十餘日。

translations.literal: ----10 The Emperor was ill, loathed seeing people, lay within the forbidden apartments, and edicted that doorkeepers were not to admit the ministers; the ministers Zhou Bo, Guan Ying, and others dared not enter—for more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: ----10 The Emperor fell ill, loathed seeing anyone, and lay in the inner palace; he ordered doorkeepers not to admit ministers, and for more than ten days Zhou Bo, Guan Ying, and the rest dared not enter.

sentences.zh: 舞陽侯樊噲排闥直入，大臣隨之。

translations.literal: Marquis of Wuyang, Fan Kuai, pushed open the side door and entered straight in; the great ministers followed.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Wuyang Fan Kuai pushed through the side door and went straight in, and the great ministers followed.

sentences.zh: 上獨枕一宦者臥。

translations.literal: The Emperor lay alone with his head on one eunuch's lap.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor lay alone with his head pillowed on a eunuch.

sentences.zh: 噲等見上，流涕曰：「始陛下與臣等起豐、沛，定天下，何其壯也？

translations.literal: Fan Kuai and the others, seeing the Emperor, wept and said, “At first Your Majesty rose with us from Feng and Pei and settled the realm—how stalwart that was!
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Kuai and the others saw him they wept and said, “When Your Majesty rose with us from Feng and Pei and settled the realm, how stalwart you were!

sentences.zh: 今天下已定，又何憊也？

translations.literal: Now the realm is settled—why so weary?
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is settled—why so weary?

sentences.zh: 且陛下病甚，大臣震恐；

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty is gravely ill and the great ministers are shaken with fear;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is gravely ill and the ministers are terrified;

sentences.zh: 不見臣等計事，顧獨與一宦者絕乎？

translations.literal: you will not see us to plan affairs, yet would cut yourself off alone with one eunuch?
translations.idiomatic: you will not see us to plan affairs, yet shut yourself off with a single eunuch?

sentences.zh: 且陛下獨不見趙高之事乎？

translations.literal: Has Your Majesty alone not seen what happened with Zhao Gao?
translations.idiomatic: Has Your Majesty forgotten what happened with Zhao Gao?

sentences.zh: 」帝笑而起。

translations.literal: ” The Emperor laughed and rose.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Emperor laughed and got up.

sentences.zh: ----11秋，七月，淮南王布反。

translations.literal: ----11 In autumn, the seventh month, the King of Huainan, Bu, rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: ----11 In autumn, the seventh month, King Bu of Huainan rebelled.

sentences.zh: 初，淮陰侯死，布已心恐。

translations.literal: At first, when the Marquis of Huaiyin died, Bu was already fearful at heart.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Marquis of Huaiyin was executed, Bu was already afraid.

sentences.zh: 及彭越誅，醢其肉以賜諸侯。

translations.literal: When Peng Yue was executed, his flesh was made into paste and bestowed on the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: When Peng Yue was executed, his flesh was minced into paste and sent to the feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 使者至淮南，淮南王方獵，見醢，因大恐，陰令人部聚兵，候伺旁郡警急。

translations.literal: When the envoy reached Huainan, the King of Huainan was just hunting; seeing the paste, he was greatly afraid and secretly ordered men to muster troops and watch neighboring commanderies for alarms.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy reached Huainan the king was hunting; seeing the paste he was terrified and secretly ordered troops gathered and watches set on neighboring commanderies.

sentences.zh: 布所幸姬病就醫，醫家與中大夫賁赫對門，赫乃厚饋遺，從姬飲醫家；

translations.literal: A favorite concubine of Bu fell ill and went to a physician; the physician's house faced that of the palace grandee Ben He, who therefore sent rich gifts and drank with the concubine at the physician's house;
translations.idiomatic: A favorite concubine of Bu fell ill and sought a physician; the physician lived opposite Palace Grandee Ben He, who sent lavish gifts and drank with the concubine at the physician's house;

sentences.zh: 王疑其與亂，欲捕赫。

translations.literal: the king suspected him of plotting disorder and wished to seize He.
translations.idiomatic: the king suspected him of plotting rebellion and meant to arrest He.

sentences.zh: 赫乘傳詣長安上變，言：「布謀反有端，可先未發誅也。

translations.literal: He took post-horses and went to Chang'an to report a crisis, saying, “Bu's plotting rebellion has clear signs; he may be executed before he rises.
translations.idiomatic: He took relay horses to Chang'an and reported: “Bu's rebellion has clear signs; he can be executed before he rises.

sentences.zh: 」上讀其書，語蕭相國，相國曰：「布不宜有此，恐仇怨妄誣之。

translations.literal: ” The Emperor read his memorial and spoke with Chancellor Xiao; the chancellor said, “Bu ought not to have this; I fear a personal enemy falsely accused him.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Emperor read his report and consulted Chancellor Xiao, who said, “Bu is unlikely to do this; I fear an enemy falsely accused him.

sentences.zh: 請系赫，使人微驗淮南王。

translations.literal: I ask that He be detained and men be sent to investigate the King of Huainan quietly.
translations.idiomatic: Detain He and send men to investigate the King of Huainan discreetly.

sentences.zh: 」淮南王布見赫以罪亡上變，固已疑其言國陰事；

translations.literal: ” The King of Huainan, Bu, seeing that He had fled after a crime to report a crisis, already suspected that he had disclosed the state's secrets;
translations.idiomatic: ” King Bu of Huainan, seeing He flee after a crime to report him, already suspected He had revealed state secrets;

sentences.zh: 漢使又來，頗有所驗；

translations.literal: Han envoys came again and found much to verify;
translations.idiomatic: Han envoys came again and found much confirmed;

sentences.zh: 遂族赫家，發兵反。

translations.literal: thereupon he destroyed He's clan by degrees and raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: so he wiped out He's clan and rose in arms.

sentences.zh: 反書聞，上乃赦賁赫，以為將軍。

translations.literal: When word of the rebellion arrived, the Emperor then pardoned Ben He and made him a general.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the rebellion arrived, the Emperor pardoned Ben He and made him a general.

sentences.zh: 上召諸將問計，皆曰：「發兵擊之，坑豎子耳，何能為乎？

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned the generals to ask their plans; all said, “Send troops to strike him—bury the brat, that's all; what can he do?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned the generals for counsel; all said, “Send troops and crush him—he's just a brat; what can he do?

sentences.zh: 」汝陰侯滕公召故楚令尹薛公問之。

translations.literal: ” Marquis of Ruyin, the Lord of Teng, summoned the former Chu prime minister, the Lord of Xue, and questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Marquis of Ruyin the Lord of Teng summoned the former Chu prime minister, the Lord of Xue, and asked him.

sentences.zh: 令尹曰：「是固當反。

translations.literal: The prime minister said, “He was bound to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: The prime minister said, “He was bound to rebel.

sentences.zh: 」滕公曰：「上裂地而封之，疏爵而王之；

translations.literal: ” The Lord of Teng said, “Your Majesty split lands and enfeoffed him, raised him in noble rank and made him a king;
translations.idiomatic: ” The Lord of Teng said, “Your Majesty carved out lands and enfeoffed him, raised his rank and made him a king;

sentences.zh: 其反何也？

translations.literal: why would he rebel?
translations.idiomatic: why would he rebel?

sentences.zh: 」令尹曰：「往年殺彭越，前年殺韓信；

translations.literal: ” The prime minister said, “Last year Peng Yue was killed; the year before, Han Xin was killed;
translations.idiomatic: ” The prime minister said, “Last year Peng Yue was killed; the year before, Han Xin;

sentences.zh: 此三人者，同功一體之人也，自疑禍及身，故反耳。

translations.literal: these three were men of the same merit and one body; suspecting that disaster would reach themselves, they rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: these three were men of equal merit and one mold; fearing disaster would reach them, they rebelled.

sentences.zh: 」滕公言之上，上乃召見，問薛公，薛公對曰：「布反不足怪也。

translations.literal: ” The Lord of Teng reported this to the Emperor; the Emperor then summoned him and questioned the Lord of Xue, who replied, “Bu's rebellion is not strange.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Lord of Teng told the Emperor, who summoned the Lord of Xue and asked him; he replied, “Bu's rebellion is no surprise.

sentences.zh: 使布出於上計，山東非漢之有也；

translations.literal: If Bu adopts the upper plan, the lands east of the mountains will not belong to Han;
translations.idiomatic: If Bu adopts the upper plan, the east will no longer belong to Han;

sentences.zh: 出於中計，勝敗之數未可知也；

translations.literal: if he adopts the middle plan, whether he wins or loses cannot yet be known;
translations.idiomatic: if the middle plan, victory and defeat are uncertain;

sentences.zh: 出於下計，陛下安枕而臥矣。

translations.literal: if he adopts the lower plan, Your Majesty may rest your head on the pillow and sleep.
translations.idiomatic: if the lower plan, Your Majesty may sleep in peace.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「何謂上計？

translations.literal: ” The Emperor said, “What is called the upper plan?
translations.idiomatic: ” The Emperor said, “What is the upper plan?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「東取吳，西取楚，並齊，取魯，傳檄燕、趙，固守其所，山東非漢之有也。

translations.literal: ” He replied, “Take Wu in the east and Chu in the west, absorb Qi, seize Lu, send proclamations to Yan and Zhao, and hold fast to what he has—the lands east of the mountains will not belong to Han.
translations.idiomatic: ” He replied, “Take Wu in the east and Chu in the west, absorb Qi, seize Lu, send proclamations to Yan and Zhao, and hold his ground—the east will no longer belong to Han.

sentences.zh: 」「何謂中計？

translations.literal: ”“What is called the middle plan?
translations.idiomatic: ”“What is the middle plan?

sentences.zh: 」「東取吳，西取楚，並韓，取魏，據敖倉之粟，塞成皋之口，勝敗之數未可行也。

translations.literal: ”“Take Wu in the east and Chu in the west, absorb Han, seize Wei, hold the grain of the Ao granary, block the mouth of Chenggao—the count of victory and defeat cannot yet be settled.
translations.idiomatic: ”“Take Wu in the east and Chu in the west, absorb Han, seize Wei, hold the Ao granary's grain, block Chenggao—the outcome cannot yet be told.

sentences.zh: 」「何謂下計？

translations.literal: ”“What is called the lower plan?
translations.idiomatic: ”“What is the lower plan?

sentences.zh: 」「東取吳，西取下蔡，歸重於越，身歸長沙，陛下安枕而臥，漢無事矣。

translations.literal: ”“Take Wu in the east and Xiapi in the west, shift his weight to Yue, return in person to Changsha—Your Majesty may rest your head on the pillow and sleep, and Han will have no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: ”“Take Wu in the east and Xiapi in the west, shift his weight to Yue, return in person to Changsha—Your Majesty may sleep in peace and Han will be untroubled.

translations.literal: ” The Emperor said, “Which plan will he adopt?
translations.idiomatic: ” The Emperor said, “Which plan will he choose?

translations.idiomatic: ” He replied, “The lower plan.

translations.literal: ” The Emperor said, “Why do you discard the upper and middle plans and choose the lower?
translations.idiomatic: ” The Emperor said, “Why abandon the upper and middle plans for the lower?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「布，故麗山之徒也，自致萬乘之主，此皆為身，不顧後、為百姓萬世慮者也。

translations.literal: ” He replied, “Bu was formerly a captive at Mount Li; he raised himself to lord of ten thousand chariots—these are men who act for themselves, who do not look to what follows or plan for the people for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: ” He replied, “Bu was once a captive at Mount Li and made himself lord of ten thousand chariots—such men act for themselves, heedless of consequences and of the people for generations to come.

translations.literal: Therefore I say he will adopt the lower plan.
translations.idiomatic: So I say he will take the lower plan.

translations.literal: ” The Emperor said, “Good!
translations.idiomatic: ” The Emperor said, “Good!
