translations.literal: ” He enfeoffed the Lord of Xue with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: ” He enfeoffed the Lord of Xue with one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 乃立皇子長為淮南王。

translations.literal: He then established the imperial son Chang as King of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He then made his son Chang King of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 是時，上有疾，欲使太子往擊黥布。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor was ill and wished to send the crown prince to attack Qing Bu.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Emperor was ill and meant to send the crown prince against Qing Bu.

sentences.zh: 太子客東園公、綺里季、夏黃公、角里先生說建成侯呂釋之曰：「太子將兵，有功則位不益，無功則從此受禍矣。

translations.literal: The crown prince's retainers Dongyuan Gong, Qili Ji, Xia Huang Gong, and Master Jueli persuaded Marquis of Jian'cheng Lü Shizhi, saying, “If the crown prince commands troops, with merit his rank will not increase, and without merit from this he will suffer disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's retainers Dongyuan Gong, Qili Ji, Xia Huang Gong, and Master Jueli urged Marquis of Jian'cheng Lü Shizhi: “If the crown prince commands troops, success will not raise his standing, and failure will bring disaster.

sentences.zh: 君何不急請呂后，承間為上泣言：『黥布，天下猛將也，善用兵。

translations.literal: Why do you not urgently ask Empress Lü, seize an occasion to weep before the Emperor, and say, ‘Qing Bu is the realm's fierce general and skilled in using troops.
translations.idiomatic: Urge Empress Lü at once to seize a moment and weep before the Emperor: ‘Qing Bu is the realm's fiercest general and a master of war.

sentences.zh: 今諸將皆陛下故等夷，乃令太子將此屬，無異使羊將狼，莫肯為用；

translations.literal: Now the generals are all Your Majesty's old equals, yet you would have the crown prince command these men—it is no different from making a sheep lead wolves; none will be willing to serve;
translations.idiomatic: The generals are all Your Majesty's old equals, yet you would put the crown prince over them—it is like setting a sheep to lead wolves; none will obey;

sentences.zh: 且使布聞之，則鼓行而西耳！

translations.literal: moreover, if Bu hears of it, he will beat his drums and march west!
translations.idiomatic: and if Bu hears of it he will beat his drums and march west at once!

sentences.zh: 上雖病，強載輜車，臥而護之，諸將不敢不盡力。

translations.literal: Though Your Majesty is ill, force yourself into the supply wagon, lie down and lead them—the generals will not dare fail to exert themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Majesty is ill, force yourself into the supply wagon and lead them lying down—the generals will not dare hold back.

sentences.zh: 上雖苦，為妻子自強！

translations.literal: Though Your Majesty suffers, strive for your wife and son!
translations.idiomatic: Though it pains you, strive on for your wife and son!

sentences.zh: 』」於是呂釋之立夜見呂后。

translations.literal: ’” Thereupon Lü Shizhi at once that night saw Empress Lü.
translations.idiomatic: ’” Thereupon Lü Shizhi went to Empress Lü that very night.

sentences.zh: 呂后承間為上泣涕而言，如四人意。

translations.literal: Empress Lü seized an occasion to weep before the Emperor and speak as the four men had wished.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Lü seized a moment, wept before the Emperor, and spoke as the four had urged.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「吾惟豎子固不足遣，而公自行耳。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, “I knew the brat was truly not fit to send; I myself will go.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, “I knew the boy was not fit to send; I will go myself.

sentences.zh: 於是上自將兵而東，群臣居守，皆送至霸上。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Emperor personally led troops east; the ministers remained to guard and all escorted him to Bashang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then led the army east in person; the ministers stayed behind and escorted him to Bashang.

sentences.zh: 留侯病，自強起，至曲郵，見上曰：「臣宜從，病甚。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Liu was ill but forced himself up; reaching Qu'e, he saw the Emperor and said, “I ought to follow, but my illness is severe.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Liu was ill but forced himself up; at Qu'e he saw the Emperor and said, “I ought to follow, but I am too ill.

sentences.zh: 楚人剽疾，願上無與爭鋒！

translations.literal: The men of Chu are swift and fierce; I wish Your Majesty would not contend with them at the spearpoint!
translations.idiomatic: The men of Chu are swift and fierce; do not meet them head-on!

sentences.zh: 」因說上令太子為將軍，監關中兵。

translations.literal: ” He therefore urged the Emperor to make the crown prince general and supervise the Guanzhong troops.
translations.idiomatic: ” He urged the Emperor to make the crown prince general and supervise the Guanzhong forces.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「子房雖病，強臥而傅太子。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, “Though Zifang is ill, force yourself to lie down and tutor the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, “Though Zifang is ill, force yourself to tutor the crown prince from your bed.

sentences.zh: 」是時，叔孫通為太傅，留侯行少傅事。

translations.literal: ” At that time Shusun Tong was grand tutor and the Marquis of Liu performed the duties of junior tutor.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shusun Tong was grand tutor and the Marquis of Liu acted as junior tutor.

sentences.zh: 發上郡、北地、隴西車騎、巴蜀材官及中尉卒三萬人為皇太子衛，軍霸上。

translations.literal: He mobilized chariots and horsemen from Shang commandery, Beidi, and Longxi, elite troops from Ba and Shu, and thirty thousand men of the commandant of the capital to guard the crown prince, encamped at Bashang.
translations.idiomatic: He mobilized chariots and cavalry from Shang, Beidi, and Longxi, elite troops from Ba and Shu, and thirty thousand capital guardsmen for the crown prince and encamped them at Bashang.

sentences.zh: 布之初反，謂其將曰：「上老矣，厭兵，必不能來。

translations.literal: When Bu first rebelled he told his generals, “The Emperor is old and weary of war; he surely cannot come.
translations.idiomatic: When Bu first rebelled he told his generals, “The Emperor is old and sick of war; he will not come.

sentences.zh: 使諸將，諸將獨患淮陰、彭越，今皆已死，餘不足畏也。

translations.literal: If he sends the generals, the generals feared only Huaiyin and Peng Yue; now both are dead—the rest are not worth fearing.
translations.idiomatic: If he sends his generals, they feared only Huaiyin and Peng Yue, and both are dead—the rest are nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 」故遂反。

translations.literal: ” Therefore he rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: ” So he rebelled.

sentences.zh: 果如薛公之言，東擊荊。

translations.literal: It turned out as the Lord of Xue had said: he struck Jing in the east.
translations.idiomatic: It turned out as the Lord of Xue had said: he attacked Jing in the east.

sentences.zh: 荊王賈走死富陵；

translations.literal: The King of Jing, Jia, fled and died at Fuling;
translations.idiomatic: King Jia of Jing fled and died at Fuling;

sentences.zh: 盡劫其兵，渡淮擊楚。

translations.literal: he seized all his troops, crossed the Huai, and attacked Chu.
translations.idiomatic: seized all his troops, crossed the Huai, and attacked Chu.

sentences.zh: 楚發兵與戰徐、僮間。

translations.literal: Chu sent troops and fought him between Xu and Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Chu sent troops and fought him between Xu and Tong.

sentences.zh: 為三軍，欲以相救為奇。

translations.literal: Chu divided into three armies, wishing to use mutual rescue as a stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Chu split into three armies, hoping mutual rescue would be their advantage.

sentences.zh: 或說楚將曰：「布善用兵，民素畏之。

translations.literal: Someone urged the Chu general, saying, “Bu is skilled in using troops and the people have long feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged the Chu commander: “Bu is skilled in war and the people have long feared him.

sentences.zh: 且兵法：『諸侯自戰其地為散地』，今別為三，彼敗吾一軍，餘皆走，安能相救！

translations.literal: Moreover the art of war says, ‘When feudal lords fight on their own ground it is scattered ground’; now you are split in three—if he defeats one of our armies the rest will all flee; how can they rescue one another!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the art of war says, ‘When lords fight on their own soil it is scattered ground’; split three ways, if he routs one army the rest will flee—how can they rescue each other!

sentences.zh: 」不聽。

translations.literal: ” He would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: ” He would not listen.

sentences.zh: 布果破其一軍，其二軍散走；

translations.literal: Bu indeed broke one army; the other two armies scattered and fled;
translations.idiomatic: Bu routed one army as predicted; the other two scattered;

sentences.zh: 布遂引兵而西。

translations.literal: Bu then led his troops west.
translations.idiomatic: Bu then marched west.

sentences.zh: 1冬，十月，上與布兵遇於蘄西，布兵精甚。

translations.literal: 1 In winter, the tenth month, the Emperor met Bu's troops at Qixi; Bu's soldiers were very keen.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In winter, the tenth month, the Emperor met Bu at Qixi; Bu's troops were very sharp.

sentences.zh: 上壁庸城，望布軍置陳如項籍軍，上惡之。

translations.literal: The Emperor fortified Yongcheng; gazing at Bu's army he saw their array set out like Xiang Yu's army, and he hated it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor fortified Yongcheng; seeing Bu's array laid out like Xiang Yu's, he was repelled.

sentences.zh: 與布相望見，遙謂布曰：「何苦而反？

translations.literal: Facing Bu at a distance he called to him, “Why toil to rebel?
translations.idiomatic: Facing Bu across the field he called, “Why rebel at such cost?

sentences.zh: 」布曰：「欲為帝耳！

translations.literal: ” Bu said, “I wish to be emperor, that's all!
translations.idiomatic: ” Bu said, “I want to be emperor, that's all!

sentences.zh: 」上怒罵之，遂大戰。

translations.literal: ” The Emperor cursed him in anger and they joined in great battle.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Emperor cursed him and they joined battle.

sentences.zh: 布軍敗走，渡淮，數止戰，不利，與百餘人走江南，上令別將追之。

translations.literal: Bu's army was defeated and fled; crossing the Huai he several times halted to fight but fared ill, and with a little more than a hundred men fled into the lands south of the Yangtze; the Emperor ordered a separate general to pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Bu's army broke and fled; crossing the Huai he fought again and again without success, and fled south of the Yangtze with a little over a hundred men while the Emperor sent other generals in pursuit.

sentences.zh: ----2上還，過沛，留，置酒沛宮，悉召故人、父老、諸母、子弟佐酒，道舊故為笑樂。

translations.literal: ----2 The Emperor returned, passed through Pei, stayed, set out wine at the Pei palace, summoned all old friends, village elders, the neighborhood mothers, and younger kin to share the wine, and spoke of old times in laughter and joy.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 On his return he passed through Pei, stayed, and held a feast at the Pei palace, calling all old friends, elders, neighborhood mothers, and younger kin to drink with him and reliving old times in laughter.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，上自為歌，起舞，慷慨傷懷，泣數行下，謂沛父兄曰：「遊子悲故鄉。

translations.literal: When the wine was deep the Emperor himself composed a song, danced, was moved with generous grief, wept several lines down his face, and told the fathers and elders of Pei, “The wanderer grieves for his homeland.
translations.idiomatic: Deep in wine the Emperor sang, danced, was moved to generous grief, wept freely, and told the elders of Pei, “The wanderer grieves for home.

sentences.zh: 朕自沛公以誅暴逆，遂有天下；

translations.literal: I from Duke of Pei punished the violent and rebellious and thereby gained the realm;
translations.idiomatic: I rose as Duke of Pei to punish the violent and rebellious and thereby gained the realm;

sentences.zh: 其以沛為朕湯沐邑，復其民，世世無有所與。

translations.literal: let Pei be my bath-and-rest fief, exempt its people, and for generation after generation grant them nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: let Pei be my personal fief, exempt its people, and never levy anything on them for all generations.

sentences.zh: 」樂飲十餘日，乃去。

translations.literal: ” They drank in joy for more than ten days before he departed.
translations.idiomatic: ” They feasted for more than ten days before he left.

sentences.zh: ----3漢別將擊英布軍洮水南、北，皆大破之。

translations.literal: ----3 Han's separate generals struck Ying Bu's army south and north of the Tao River and routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 Han's separate generals attacked Ying Bu south and north of the Tao River and routed him utterly.

sentences.zh: 布故與番君婚，以故長沙成王臣使人誘布，偽欲與亡走越，布信而隨之。

translations.literal: Bu had formerly been allied by marriage with the Lord of Pan; for this reason King Cheng of Changsha, Chen, sent men to entice Bu, falsely wishing to flee with him to Yue; Bu believed them and followed.
translations.idiomatic: Bu had once been allied by marriage to the Lord of Pan; King Cheng of Changsha, Chen, sent men to lure him, pretending they would flee together to Yue; Bu believed them and followed.

sentences.zh: 番陽人殺布茲鄉民田舍。

translations.literal: Men of Poyang killed Bu in a village field hut at Zixiang.
translations.idiomatic: Men of Poyang killed Bu in a village hut at Zixiang.

sentences.zh: ----4周勃悉定代郡、雁門、雲中地，斬陳豨於當城。

translations.literal: ----4 Zhou Bo fully settled the lands of Dai commandery, Yanmen, and Yunzhong and beheaded Chen Xi at Dangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 Zhou Bo fully pacified Dai, Yanmen, and Yunzhong and beheaded Chen Xi at Dangcheng.

sentences.zh: ----5上以荊王賈無後，更以荊為吳國。

translations.literal: ----5 Because the King of Jing, Jia, had no heir, the Emperor changed Jing into the state of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 Because King Jia of Jing had no heir, the Emperor made Jing into the state of Wu.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，立兄仲之子濞為吳王，王三郡、五十三城。

translations.literal: On xinchou he established the son of his elder brother Zhong, Liu Pi, as King of Wu, ruling three commanderies and fifty-three cities.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou he made his elder brother Zhong's son Liu Pi King of Wu, ruling three commanderies and fifty-three cities.

sentences.zh: ----6十一月，上過魯，以太牢祠孔子。

translations.literal: ----6 In the eleventh month the Emperor passed through Lu and sacrificed to Confucius with the grand offering.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 In the eleventh month the Emperor passed through Lu and sacrificed to Confucius with the grand offering.

sentences.zh: ----7上從破黥布歸，疾益甚，愈欲易太子。

translations.literal: ----7 When the Emperor returned from defeating Qing Bu his illness grew worse and he wished all the more to replace the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: ----7 When the Emperor returned from defeating Qing Bu his illness grew worse and he wished all the more to replace the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 張良諫不聽，因疾不視事。

translations.literal: Zhang Liang remonstrated but was not heeded; on account of illness he ceased attending to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liang remonstrated in vain and, pleading illness, ceased attending to affairs.

sentences.zh: 叔孫通諫曰：「昔者晉獻公以驪姬之故，廢太子，立奚齊，晉國亂者數十年，為天下笑。

translations.literal: Shusun Tong remonstrated, saying, “Formerly Duke Xian of Jin, on account of Lady Li, deposed the crown prince and established Xi Qi; Jin was in disorder for several decades and became the laughingstock of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Shusun Tong remonstrated: “Formerly Duke Xian of Jin, for Lady Li's sake, deposed his heir and made Xi Qi crown prince; Jin was torn by disorder for decades and became the world's laughingstock.

sentences.zh: 秦以不蚤定扶蘇，令趙高得以詐立胡亥，自使滅祀，此陛下所親見。

translations.literal: Qin, because it did not early settle Fusu, allowed Zhao Gao to establish Huhai by fraud and thereby destroyed its sacrifices—this Your Majesty has seen with your own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Qin, because it did not settle Fusu early, let Zhao Gao install Huhai by fraud and destroy its line—Your Majesty saw this yourself.

sentences.zh: 今太子仁孝，天下皆聞之。

translations.literal: Now the crown prince is benevolent and filial; all the realm has heard of it.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is benevolent and filial; all the realm knows it.

sentences.zh: 呂后與陛下攻苦食淡，其可背哉？

translations.literal: The Empress Lü and Your Majesty endured hardship and ate plain food—how could one turn one's back on that?
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Lü and Your Majesty endured hardship and ate plain fare—how could one betray that?

sentences.zh: 陛下必欲廢適而立少，臣願先伏誅，以頸血污地。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty must depose the heir and establish the younger son, your servant is willing to submit first to execution and stain the ground with the blood of his neck.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty must depose the heir and install the younger son, your servant begs to die first and stain the ground with his neck's blood.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「公罷矣，吾直戲耳。

translations.literal: ” The Emperor said, “Stop, sir; I was only jesting.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Emperor said, “Enough, sir—I was only jesting.

sentences.zh: 」叔孫通曰：「太子，天下本，本一搖，天下振動；

translations.literal: ” Shusun Tong said, “The crown prince is the root of the realm; if the root shakes once, the realm trembles;
translations.idiomatic: ” Shusun Tong said, “The crown prince is the root of the realm; shake the root once and the realm trembles;

sentences.zh: 奈何以天下為戲乎？

translations.literal: how can you take the realm as a jest?
translations.idiomatic: how can you treat the realm as a jest?

sentences.zh: 」時大臣固爭者多；

translations.literal: ” At that time many great ministers firmly remonstrated;
translations.idiomatic: ” Many great ministers remonstrated firmly;

sentences.zh: 上知群臣心皆不附趙王，乃止不立。

translations.literal: the Emperor knew that in the ministers' hearts none favored the King of Zhao, and therefore stopped and did not install him.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor saw that none of the ministers favored the King of Zhao and dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: ----8相國何以長安地狹，上林中多空地，棄；

translations.literal: ----8 The Chancellor, on account of Chang'an's narrow territory, [said that] in the Shanglin park there was much vacant land lying waste;
translations.idiomatic: ----8 The Chancellor, because Chang'an's territory was cramped, [said that] much land in the Shanglin park lay vacant and wasted;

sentences.zh: 願令民得入田，毋收蒿，為禽獸食。

translations.literal: he wished to let the people enter and farm it, collecting no brushwood fees, [so it would be] food for birds and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: he wished to let the people farm it without brushwood fees, for birds and beasts to feed on.

sentences.zh: 上大怒曰：「相國多受賈人財物，乃為請吾苑！

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly angry and said, “The Chancellor has received much property from merchants and thus petitions My park for them!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious: “The Chancellor has taken so much from merchants that he petitions My park for them!

sentences.zh: 」下相國廷尉，械系之。

translations.literal: ” He sent the Chancellor down to the commandant of justice and shackled and detained him.
translations.idiomatic: ” He sent the Chancellor to the commandant of justice and had him shackled and detained.

sentences.zh: 數日，王衛尉侍，前問曰：「相國何大罪，陛下系之暴也？

translations.literal: Several days later, Wang the commandant of the guard attended and stepped forward asking, “What great crime has the Chancellor committed that Your Majesty detained him so harshly?
translations.idiomatic: Days later Wang the commandant of the guard attended and asked, “What great crime has the Chancellor committed that Your Majesty detained him so harshly?

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「吾聞李斯相秦皇帝，有善歸主，有惡自與。

translations.literal: ” The Emperor said, “I have heard that when Li Si served as chancellor to the First Emperor of Qin, what was good he attributed to the ruler and what was bad he took on himself.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Emperor said, “I have heard that when Li Si served the First Emperor of Qin, he credited the ruler with good and took blame on himself.

sentences.zh: 今相國多受賈豎金，而為之請吾苑以媚於民，故系治之。

translations.literal: Now the Chancellor has received much gold from merchant fellows and petitions My park on their behalf to curry favor with the people—therefore I detained and tried him.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Chancellor has taken much gold from merchants and petitions My park to curry favor with the people—that is why I detained him.

sentences.zh: 」王衛尉曰：「夫職事苟有便於民而請之，真宰相事；

translations.literal: ” Wang the commandant of the guard said, “If official duties happen to benefit the people and one petitions for that, it is truly a chancellor's business;
translations.idiomatic: ” Wang the commandant of the guard said, “If an official duty benefits the people and one petitions for it, that is truly a chancellor's work;

sentences.zh: 陛下奈何乃疑相國受賈人錢乎？

translations.literal: how can Your Majesty suspect the Chancellor of receiving merchants' money?
translations.idiomatic: why should Your Majesty suspect the Chancellor of taking merchants' money?

sentences.zh: 且陛下距楚數歲，陳豨、黥布反，陛下自將而往；

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty was several years from Chu; when Chen Xi and Qing Bu rebelled, Your Majesty personally led [troops] and went;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Your Majesty was years away fighting in Chu; when Chen Xi and Qing Bu rebelled, Your Majesty led the army in person;

sentences.zh: 當是時，相國守關中，關中搖足，則關以西非陛下有也！

translations.literal: at that time the Chancellor guarded Guanzhong—if Guanzhong stamped its foot, the lands west of the pass would no longer be Your Majesty's!
translations.idiomatic: then the Chancellor held Guanzhong—if Guanzhong stirred, everything west of the pass would no longer be Yours!

sentences.zh: 相國不以此時為利，今乃利賈人之金乎？

translations.literal: The Chancellor did not seek profit then—would he now profit from merchants' gold?
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor did not profit then—would he profit from merchants' gold now?

sentences.zh: 且秦以不聞其過亡天下；

translations.literal: Moreover Qin lost the realm because its faults were not heard;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Qin lost the realm because its faults went unheard;

sentences.zh: 李斯之分過，又何足法哉？

translations.literal: Li Si's apportioning of faults—how is that worth taking as a model?
translations.idiomatic: Li Si's way of shifting blame—what is there to emulate?

sentences.zh: 陛下何疑宰相之淺也！

translations.literal: How shallow is Your Majesty's suspicion of the chancellor!
translations.idiomatic: How shallow Your Majesty's suspicion of the chancellor!

sentences.zh: 」帝不懌。

translations.literal: ” The Emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 是日，使使持節赦出相國。

translations.literal: That day he sent an envoy bearing credentials to pardon and release the Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: That day he sent an envoy with credentials to pardon and release the Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 相國年老，素恭謹，入，徒跣謝。

translations.literal: The Chancellor was old and always respectful and cautious; entering, he went barefoot to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor was old and always deferential; he came in barefoot to apologize.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「相國休矣！

translations.literal: The Emperor said, “Chancellor, rest!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, “Chancellor, enough!

sentences.zh: 相國為民請苑，吾不許，我不過為桀、紂王，而相國為賢相。

translations.literal: The Chancellor petitioned for the park on the people's behalf and I did not grant it—I would have been no more than kings Jie and Zhou, while the Chancellor is a worthy chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor petitioned the park for the people and I refused—I would have been no better than Jie and Zhou, while the Chancellor proved himself worthy.

sentences.zh: 吾故系相國，欲令百姓聞吾過也。

translations.literal: I therefore detained the Chancellor, wishing to let the common people hear of My fault.
translations.idiomatic: I detained the Chancellor so the people would hear of My fault.

sentences.zh: 」----9陳豨之反也，燕王綰發兵擊其東北。

translations.literal: ” ----9 When Chen Xi rebelled, the King of Yan, Liu Wan, sent troops to attack his northeast.
translations.idiomatic: ” ----9 When Chen Xi rebelled, King Liu Wan of Yan sent troops against his northeast.

sentences.zh: 當是時，陳豨使王黃求救匈奴；

translations.literal: At that time Chen Xi sent Wang Huang to beg rescue from the Xiongnu;
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chen Xi sent Wang Huang to beg the Xiongnu for aid;

sentences.zh: 燕王綰亦使其臣張勝於匈奴，言豨等軍破。

translations.literal: the King of Yan also sent his minister Zhang Sheng to the Xiongnu, saying Chen Xi's army was broken.
translations.idiomatic: King Liu Wan of Yan also sent his minister Zhang Sheng to the Xiongnu, reporting that Chen Xi's forces were broken.

sentences.zh: 張勝至胡，故燕王藏荼子衍出亡在胡，見張勝曰：「公所以重於燕者，以習胡事也；

translations.literal: Zhang Sheng reached the Hu; Yan, the former King of Yan Zang Tu's son Yan, who had fled and was in exile among the Hu, saw Zhang Sheng and said, “The reason you are valued in Yan is that you are versed in Hu affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sheng reached the Hu; Yan, son of the former King of Yan Zang Tu, who had fled into exile among the Hu, saw Zhang Sheng and said, “You are valued in Yan because you know Hu affairs;

sentences.zh: 燕所以久存者，以諸侯數反，兵連不決也。

translations.literal: Yan has long survived because the feudal lords have repeatedly rebelled and war drags on unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: Yan has lasted because the lords rebel again and again and war drags on without end.

sentences.zh: 今公為燕，欲急滅豨等；

translations.literal: Now you act for Yan and wish to hurry to destroy Chen Xi and the rest;
translations.idiomatic: Now you act for Yan and wish to destroy Chen Xi and his men at once;

sentences.zh: 豨等已盡，次亦至燕，公等亦且為虜矣。

translations.literal: when Chen Xi and the rest are finished, next it will reach Yan—you too will soon be captives.
translations.idiomatic: when they are gone, Yan will be next—and you will soon be captives yourselves.

sentences.zh: 公何不令燕且緩陳豨，而與胡和？

translations.literal: Why do you not have Yan for the present ease off on Chen Xi and make peace with the Hu?
translations.idiomatic: Why not have Yan hold back against Chen Xi for now and make peace with the Hu?

sentences.zh: 事寬，得長王燕；

translations.literal: If matters are relaxed, you can long rule Yan;
translations.idiomatic: If matters ease, you can rule Yan for long;

sentences.zh: 即有漢急，可以安國。

translations.literal: if there is urgency from Han, you can secure the state.
translations.idiomatic: if Han presses hard, you can still secure your state.

sentences.zh: 」張勝以為然，乃私令匈奴助豨等擊燕。

translations.literal: ” Zhang Sheng thought it right and secretly ordered the Xiongnu to help Chen Xi and the rest attack Yan.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhang Sheng agreed and secretly ordered the Xiongnu to help Chen Xi attack Yan.

sentences.zh: 燕王綰疑張勝與胡反，上書請族張勝。

translations.literal: The King of Yan suspected Zhang Sheng of turning against him with the Hu and memorialized asking to execute Zhang Sheng's clan by degrees.
translations.idiomatic: King Liu Wan suspected Zhang Sheng of colluding with the Hu and memorialized to wipe out Zhang Sheng's clan.

sentences.zh: 勝還，具道所以為者；

translations.literal: Sheng returned and fully explained why he had done it;
translations.idiomatic: Sheng returned and explained fully what he had done;

sentences.zh: 燕王乃詐論他人，脫勝家屬，使得為匈奴間。

translations.literal: the King of Yan then falsely indicted others, exonerated Sheng's kin, and let him serve as a spy for the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: the king then framed others, freed Sheng's kin, and let him serve as a Xiongnu spy.

sentences.zh: 而陰使范齊之陳豨所，欲令久亡，連兵勿決。

translations.literal: and secretly sent Fan Qi to Chen Xi's camp, wishing to make the war long unsettled and the armies linked without resolution.
translations.idiomatic: and secretly sent Fan Qi to Chen Xi's camp to prolong the war and keep the armies locked without decision.

sentences.zh: 漢擊黥布，豨常將兵居代；

translations.literal: When Han attacked Qing Bu, Xi often held troops stationed in Dai;
translations.idiomatic: While Han attacked Qing Bu, Xi often held troops in Dai;

sentences.zh: 漢擊斬豨，其裨將降，言燕王綰使范齊通計謀於豨所。

translations.literal: when Han attacked and beheaded Xi, his lieutenant general surrendered and said the King of Yan Liu Wan had sent Fan Qi to pass plans with Xi.
translations.idiomatic: when Han attacked and killed Xi, a lieutenant general surrendered and said King Liu Wan of Yan had sent Fan Qi to Chen Xi with plans.

sentences.zh: 帝使使召盧綰，綰稱病；

translations.literal: The Emperor sent an envoy to summon Liu Wan; Wan claimed illness;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent to summon Liu Wan; Wan claimed illness;

sentences.zh: 上又使辟陽侯審食其、御史大夫趙堯往迎燕王，因驗問左右。

translations.literal: the Emperor again sent Marquis of Piyang Shen Yishi and the grand secretary Zhao Yao to go and welcome the King of Yan, and thereby investigate and question those around him.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor again sent Marquis of Piyang Shen Yishi and Grand Secretary Zhao Yao to welcome the King of Yan and question his attendants.

sentences.zh: 綰愈恐，閉匿，謂其幸臣曰：「非劉氏而王，獨我與長沙耳。

translations.literal: Wan grew ever more afraid, shut himself in hiding, and said to his favored ministers, “Of those made kings who are not of the Liu clan, only I and Changsha remain.
translations.idiomatic: Wan grew more afraid, shut himself away, and told his favorites, “Of non-Liu kings, only I and Changsha remain.

sentences.zh: 往年春，漢族淮陰，夏，誅彭越，皆呂氏計。

translations.literal: In spring of the past year Han destroyed the clan of Huaiyin by degrees; in summer Peng Yue was executed—all Lü clan schemes.
translations.idiomatic: Last spring Han wiped out Huaiyin's clan; in summer Peng Yue was executed—all the Lü clan's doing.

sentences.zh: 令上病，屬任呂后；

translations.literal: The Emperor is ill and entrusts affairs to Empress Lü;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor is ill and has entrusted power to Empress Lü;

sentences.zh: 呂后婦人，專欲以事誅異姓王者及大功臣。

translations.literal: Empress Lü is a woman and aims solely to use occasions to execute kings of other surnames and great merit-holders.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Lü is a woman bent on finding pretexts to kill non-Liu kings and great merit-holders.

sentences.zh: 」乃遂稱病不行，其左右皆亡匿。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he claimed illness and would not go; his attendants all fled and hid.
translations.idiomatic: ” He then pleaded illness and would not go; his attendants all fled into hiding.

sentences.zh: 語頗洩，辟陽侯聞之，歸，具報上，上益怒。

translations.literal: Word leaked somewhat; Shen Yishi heard, returned, and fully reported to the Emperor; the Emperor grew angrier.
translations.idiomatic: Word leaked; Shen Yishi heard, returned, and reported in full; the Emperor grew angrier.

sentences.zh: 又得匈奴降者，言張勝亡在匈奴為燕使。

translations.literal: He also obtained a Xiongnu defector who said Zhang Sheng had fled to the Xiongnu and served as Yan's envoy.
translations.idiomatic: A Xiongnu defector also said Zhang Sheng had fled to the Xiongnu as Yan's envoy.

sentences.zh: 於是上曰：「盧綰果反矣！

translations.literal: Thereupon the Emperor said, “Liu Wan has truly rebelled!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then said, “Liu Wan has truly rebelled!

sentences.zh: 」春，二月，使樊噲以相國將兵擊綰，立皇子建為燕王。

translations.literal: ” In spring, the second month, he sent Fan Kuai as chancellor commanding troops to attack Wan and established the imperial son Jian as King of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: ” In spring, the second month, he sent Fan Kuai as chancellor to attack Wan and made his son Jian King of Yan.

sentences.zh: ----10詔曰：「南武侯織，亦粵之世也，立以為南海王。

translations.literal: ----10 An edict said, “Marquis of Nanwu Zhi is also of Yue's line; establish him as King of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: ----10 An edict said, “Marquis of Nanwu Zhi is also of Yue's line; establish him as King of Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 」----11上擊布時，為流矢所中，行道，疾甚。

translations.literal: ” ----11 When the Emperor attacked Bu he was struck by a stray arrow; on the march his illness grew severe.
translations.idiomatic: ” ----11 When the Emperor attacked Bu he was struck by a stray arrow; on the march his illness grew grave.

sentences.zh: 呂后迎良醫。

translations.literal: Empress Lü summoned a skilled physician.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Lü summoned a skilled physician.

sentences.zh: 醫入見，曰：「疾可治。

translations.literal: The physician entered and saw him and said, “The illness can be cured.
translations.idiomatic: The physician came in and said, “The illness can be cured.

sentences.zh: 」上嫚罵之曰：「吾以布衣提三尺取天下，此非天命乎？

translations.literal: ” The Emperor scornfully reviled him, saying, “I took the realm in plain cloth raising three feet [of steel]—is this not Heaven's mandate?
translations.idiomatic: ” The Emperor scornfully cursed him: “I took the realm as a commoner with a three-foot sword—is that not Heaven's mandate?

sentences.zh: 命乃在天，雖扁鵲何益？

translations.literal: Fate is in Heaven—what use even Bian Que?
translations.idiomatic: Fate lies with Heaven—what use is even Bian Que?

sentences.zh: 」遂不使治疾，賜黃金五十斤，罷之。

translations.literal: ” He then would not let him treat the illness, bestowed fifty jin of gold, and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: ” He would not let him treat the illness, gave him fifty jin of gold, and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 呂后問曰：「陛下百歲後，蕭相國既死，誰令代之？

translations.literal: Empress Lü asked, “After Your Majesty's hundred years, when Chancellor Xiao is dead, who shall replace him?
translations.idiomatic: Empress Lü asked, “After Your Majesty passes, when Chancellor Xiao is gone, who should replace him?

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「曹參可。

translations.literal: ” The Emperor said, “Cao Shen will do.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Emperor said, “Cao Shen.

sentences.zh: 」問其次，曰：「王陵可，然少戇，陳平可以助之。

translations.literal: ” Asked for the next, he said, “Wang Ling will do, but he is somewhat blunt and simple; Chen Ping can assist him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Asked who was next, he said, “Wang Ling, though he is somewhat blunt; Chen Ping can assist him.

sentences.zh: 陳平知有餘，然難獨任。

translations.literal: Chen Ping's knowledge has surplus, yet he is hard to entrust alone.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ping's talents exceed what is needed, yet he is hard to entrust alone.

sentences.zh: 周勃重厚少文，然安劉氏者必勃也，可令為太尉。

translations.literal: Zhou Bo is weighty, thick, and short on polish, yet he who will secure the Liu clan must be Bo; he may be made grand commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Bo is stolid and unpolished, yet whoever secures the Liu clan will be Bo; make him grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 」呂后復問其次，上曰：「此後亦非乃所知也。

translations.literal: ” Empress Lü again asked for the next; the Emperor said, “Beyond this is not for you to know.
translations.idiomatic: ” Empress Lü asked again; the Emperor said, “Beyond that is not for you to know.

sentences.zh: 」夏，四月，甲辰，帝崩於長樂宮。

translations.literal: ” In summer, the fourth month, on jiachen the Emperor died at Changle Palace.
translations.idiomatic: ” In summer, the fourth month, on jiachen the Emperor died at Changle Palace.

sentences.zh: 丁未，發喪，大赦天下。

translations.literal: On dingwei the mourning was proclaimed and a great amnesty was granted to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei mourning was proclaimed and the realm was granted a great amnesty.

sentences.zh: ----12盧綰與數千人居塞下候伺，幸上疾愈，自入謝。

translations.literal: ----12 Liu Wan with several thousand men dwelt below the passes watching, hoping the Emperor's illness would heal so he could enter in person to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: ----12 Liu Wan with several thousand men waited below the passes, hoping the Emperor would recover so he could come in person to apologize.

sentences.zh: 聞帝崩，遂亡入匈奴。

translations.literal: Hearing the Emperor had died, he then fled and entered the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the Emperor had died, he fled into the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: ----13五月，丙寅，葬高帝於長陵。

translations.literal: ----13 In the fifth month, on bingyin, the High Emperor was buried at Changling.
translations.idiomatic: ----13 In the fifth month, on bingyin, the High Emperor was buried at Changling.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖不修文學，而性明達，好謀，能聽，自監門、戍卒，見之如舊。

translations.literal: At first, the High Ancestor did not cultivate literary learning, yet his nature was clear and penetrating; he loved counsel, could listen, and from gatekeepers to garrison soldiers, seeing them was as of old.
translations.idiomatic: At first the High Ancestor did not cultivate letters, yet he was clear-sighted, loved counsel, and listened well; from gatekeepers to garrison soldiers he treated old acquaintances as before.

sentences.zh: 初順民心作三章之約。

translations.literal: At first he followed the people's hearts in making the Three-Article Covenant.
translations.idiomatic: At first he followed the people's will in making the Three-Article Covenant.

sentences.zh: 天下既定，命蕭何次律、令，韓信申軍法，張蒼定章程，叔孫通制禮儀；

translations.literal: When the realm was settled he ordered Xiao He to arrange laws and ordinances, Han Xin to set forth military law, Zhang Cang to fix regulations and statutes, and Shusun Tong to establish ritual observances;
translations.idiomatic: When the realm was settled he had Xiao He compile laws and ordinances, Han Xin set forth military law, Zhang Cang fix regulations and statutes, and Shusun Tong establish ritual observances;

sentences.zh: 又與功臣剖符作誓，丹書、鐵契，金匱、石室，藏之宗廟。

translations.literal: he also with the merit-holders split tally-fish and made oaths—red writing on iron contracts, gold caskets and stone chambers—and stored them in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: he also split tally-fish with the merit-holders and swore oaths—red writing on iron contracts, gold caskets and stone chambers—and stored them in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 雖日不暇給，規摹弘遠矣。

translations.literal: Though day by day there was no leisure, the plan and measure were vast and far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: Though day by day left no leisure, the design was vast and far-reaching.

sentences.zh: ----14己巳，太子即皇帝位，尊皇后曰皇太后。

translations.literal: ----14 On jisi the crown prince assumed the imperial throne and honored the empress as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: ----14 On jisi the crown prince took the throne and honored the empress as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: ----15初，高帝病甚，人有惡樊噲，云：「黨於呂氏，即一日上晏駕，欲以兵誅趙王如意之屬。

translations.literal: ----15 At first, when the High Emperor was gravely ill, someone spoke ill of Fan Kuai, saying, “He is partisan to the Lü clan; if one day the Emperor passes, he wishes with troops to execute the King of Zhao Ruyi and his sort.
translations.idiomatic: ----15 When the High Emperor was gravely ill, someone slandered Fan Kuai, saying, “He sides with the Lü clan; when the Emperor passes he means to use troops to kill King Ruyi of Zhao and his kin.

sentences.zh: 」帝大怒，用陳平謀，召絳侯周勃受詔床下，曰：「陳平亟馳傳載勃代噲將；

translations.literal: ” The Emperor was greatly angry; using Chen Ping's plan he summoned Marquis of Jiang Zhou Bo to receive the edict beneath the bed, saying, “Chen Ping, speed relay horses, take Bo and replace Kuai as general;
translations.idiomatic: ” The Emperor was furious; using Chen Ping's plan he summoned Marquis of Jiang Zhou Bo to take the edict beneath the bed: “Chen Ping, take relay horses at once, bring Bo, and replace Kuai as general;

sentences.zh: 平至軍中，即斬噲頭！

translations.literal: when Ping reaches the army, at once behead Kuai!
translations.idiomatic: when Ping reaches the army, behead Kuai at once!

sentences.zh: 」二人既受詔，馳傳，未至軍，行計之曰：「樊噲，帝之故人也，功多，且又呂后弟呂嬃之夫，有親且貴。

translations.literal: ” The two, having received the edict, galloped relay; before reaching the army, en route they calculated, saying, “Fan Kuai is an old man of the Emperor's, his merit great, and moreover husband to Empress Lü's brother Lü Xu'ou's daughter—close kin and noble.
translations.idiomatic: ” The two took the edict and galloped relay; before reaching the army they reasoned: “Fan Kuai is an old companion of the Emperor, his merit great, and husband to Empress Lü's brother Lü Xu'ou's daughter—close kin and high in rank.

sentences.zh: 帝以仇怒故欲斬之，則恐後悔；

translations.literal: The Emperor, from enmity and anger, wishes to behead him—then we fear he will regret it;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, in anger and enmity, wants him killed—we fear he will regret it;

sentences.zh: 寧囚而致上，上自誅之。

translations.literal: better to imprison him and present him to the Emperor; the Emperor himself will execute him.
translations.idiomatic: better to imprison him and present him to the Emperor and let the Emperor kill him himself.

sentences.zh: 」未至軍，為壇，以節召樊噲。

translations.literal: ” Before reaching the army they made an altar and with credentials summoned Fan Kuai.
translations.idiomatic: ” Before reaching the army they built an altar and summoned Fan Kuai with credentials.

sentences.zh: 噲受詔，即反接，載檻車傳詣長安；

translations.literal: Kuai received the edict and at once was bound arms back, loaded on a caged cart, and relayed to Chang'an;
translations.idiomatic: Kuai received the edict and was bound at once, loaded on a caged cart, and relayed to Chang'an;

sentences.zh: 而令絳侯勃代將，將兵定燕反縣。

translations.literal: and they ordered Marquis of Jiang Bo to replace him as general and lead troops to settle the rebel counties of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: and had Marquis of Jiang Bo replace him and lead troops to pacify Yan's rebel counties.

sentences.zh: 平行，聞帝崩，畏呂嬃讒之於太后，乃馳傳先去。

translations.literal: Ping traveled on; hearing the Emperor had died, fearing Lü Xu'ou would slander him to the empress dowager, he galloped relay and went ahead first.
translations.idiomatic: Ping went on; hearing the Emperor had died, fearing Lü Xu'ou would slander him to the empress dowager, he galloped ahead by relay.

sentences.zh: 逢使者，詔平與灌嬰屯滎陽。

translations.literal: Meeting an envoy, [received] an edict [for] Ping and Guan Ying to garrison Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He met an envoy with an edict for Ping and Guan Ying to garrison Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 平受詔，立復馳至宮，哭殊悲；

translations.literal: Ping received the edict, at once galloped again to the palace, and wept exceedingly sadly;
translations.idiomatic: Ping took the edict, galloped straight back to the palace, and wept with extraordinary grief;

sentences.zh: 因固請得宿衛中。

translations.literal: thereby firmly requesting to be lodged in the inner guard.
translations.idiomatic: and firmly asked to lodge in the inner guard.

sentences.zh: 太后乃以為郎中令，使傅教惠帝。

translations.literal: The empress dowager then made him director of the palace gentlemen and had him tutor and teach Emperor Hui.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager then made him director of the palace gentlemen to tutor and instruct Emperor Hui.

sentences.zh: 是後呂嬃讒乃不得行。

translations.literal: After this Lü Xu'ou's slander could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: After that Lü Xu'ou's slander could not proceed.

sentences.zh: 樊噲至，則赦，復爵邑。

translations.literal: Fan Kuai arrived and was then pardoned; his noble rank and fief were restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Kuai arrived he was pardoned and his rank and fief restored.

sentences.zh: ----16太后令永巷囚戚夫人，髡鉗，衣赭衣，令舂。

translations.literal: ----16 The empress dowager ordered Lady Qi imprisoned in the everlasting alleys, shorn and shackled, clad in ochre robes, and made to pound grain.
translations.idiomatic: ----16 The empress dowager had Lady Qi imprisoned in the everlasting alleys, shorn and shackled, dressed in ochre robes, and set to pounding grain.

sentences.zh: 遣使召趙王如意。

translations.literal: She sent an envoy to summon the King of Zhao, Ruyi.
translations.idiomatic: She sent an envoy to summon King Ruyi of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 使者三反，趙相周昌謂使者曰：「高帝屬臣趙王，趙王年少，竊聞太后怨戚夫人，欲召趙王並誅之，臣不敢遣王。

translations.literal: The envoy returned three times; the chancellor of Zhao Zhou Chang told the envoy, “The High Emperor entrusted the King of Zhao to me; the King of Zhao is young. I privately hear the empress dowager resents Lady Qi and wishes to summon the King of Zhao and execute him together—I dare not send the king.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy came three times; Chancellor of Zhao Zhou Chang told him, “The High Emperor entrusted the King of Zhao to me; the king is young. I hear the empress dowager resents Lady Qi and means to summon the King of Zhao and kill him with her—I dare not send the king.

sentences.zh: 王且亦病，不能奉詔。

translations.literal: The king is moreover ill and cannot obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The king is also ill and cannot obey the edict.

sentences.zh: 」太后怒，先使人召昌。

translations.literal: ” The Empress Dowager was angry and first sent men to summon Chang.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Empress Dowager was furious and first sent men to summon Zhou Chang.

sentences.zh: 昌至長安，乃使人復召趙王。

translations.literal: When Chang reached Chang'an, she then sent men again to summon the King of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chang reached Chang'an, she sent men again to summon the King of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 王來，未到；

translations.literal: The king came but had not yet arrived;
translations.idiomatic: The king set out but had not yet arrived;

sentences.zh: 帝知太后怒，自迎趙王霸上，與入宮，自挾與起居飲食。

translations.literal: the Emperor, knowing the Empress Dowager was angry, went himself to meet the King of Zhao at Bashang, entered the palace with him, and personally held him close in rising, resting, eating, and drinking.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor, knowing the Empress Dowager was angry, went himself to meet the King of Zhao at Bashang, brought him into the palace, and personally kept him at his side day and night for meals and daily life.

sentences.zh: 太后欲殺之，不得間。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager wished to kill him but found no opening.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager wished to kill him but found no opportunity.

sentences.zh: 1冬，十二月，帝晨出射。

translations.literal: 1 In winter, the twelfth month, the Emperor went out early to shoot.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In winter, the twelfth month, the Emperor went out early to hunt.

sentences.zh: 趙王少，不能蚤起；

translations.literal: The King of Zhao was young and could not rise early;
translations.idiomatic: The King of Zhao was young and could not rise early;

sentences.zh: 太后使人持鴆飲之。

translations.literal: the Empress Dowager sent men bearing poison wine to make him drink it.
translations.idiomatic: the Empress Dowager sent men with poisoned wine and made him drink it.

sentences.zh: 犁明，帝還，趙王已死。

translations.literal: At dawn the Emperor returned; the King of Zhao was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the Emperor returned and found the King of Zhao already dead.

sentences.zh: 太后遂斷戚夫人手足，去眼，煇耳，飲喑藥，使居廁中，命曰「人彘」。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager then cut off Lady Qi's hands and feet, removed her eyes, scorched her ears, made her drink a mute drug, and had her dwell in the privy, naming her “human swine.”
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager then cut off Lady Qi's hands and feet, gouged out her eyes, deafened her ears, forced a drug that left her mute, and had her kept in the privy, calling her “the human swine.”

sentences.zh: 居數日，乃召帝觀人彘。

translations.literal: After several days she summoned the Emperor to view the human swine.
translations.idiomatic: After several days she summoned the Emperor to see the human swine.

sentences.zh: 帝見，問知其戚夫人，乃大哭，因病，歲餘不能起。

translations.literal: The Emperor saw her, asked and knew it was Lady Qi, then wept greatly, fell ill, and for more than a year could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor saw her, learned it was Lady Qi, and wept bitterly; he fell ill and for more than a year could not get up.

sentences.zh: 使人請太后曰：「此非人所為。

translations.literal: He sent someone to tell the Empress Dowager, saying, “This is not what a human being would do.
translations.idiomatic: He sent someone to tell the Empress Dowager: “This is not what a human being would do.

sentences.zh: 臣為太后子，終不能治天下。

translations.literal: I am Your Majesty's son as empress, yet in the end I cannot govern All under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I am Your Majesty's son, yet in the end I cannot govern the realm.

sentences.zh: 」帝以此日飲為淫樂，不聽政。

translations.literal: ” From that day the Emperor took drink as dissolute pleasure and would not attend to government.
translations.idiomatic: ” From that day the Emperor drowned himself in wine and pleasure and ceased to attend to government.

sentences.zh: ::臣光曰：為人子者，父母有過則諫；

translations.literal: :: Your servant Guang says: As a son, when parents have faults one should remonstrate;
translations.idiomatic: :: Your servant Guang says: As a son, when parents err one should remonstrate;

sentences.zh: 諫而不聽，則號泣而隨之。

translations.literal: if remonstrance is not heeded, then weep and wail and follow them.
translations.idiomatic: if they will not listen, then weep and follow them.

sentences.zh: 安有守高祖之業，為天下之主，不忍母之殘酷，遂棄國家而不恤，縱酒色以傷生？

translations.literal: How can one hold fast to the High Ancestor's enterprise, be lord of All under Heaven, be unable to bear his mother's cruelty, then cast aside the state without care and indulge in wine and women to harm one's life?
translations.idiomatic: How can one hold the High Ancestor's legacy, be lord of the realm, unable to bear his mother's cruelty, then abandon the state without a thought and indulge in wine and women to ruin one's health?

sentences.zh: 若孝惠者，可謂篤於小仁而未知大誼也。

translations.literal: One such as Emperor Hui may be called deep in petty benevolence yet ignorant of great principle.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui may be called devoted to petty kindness yet ignorant of great duty.

sentences.zh: ----2徙淮陽王友為趙王。

translations.literal: ----2 The King of Huaiyang, You, was moved to be King of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 King You of Huaiyang was transferred to be King of Zhao.

sentences.zh: ----3春，正月，始作長安城西北方。

translations.literal: ----3 In spring, the first month, work began on the northwest section of Chang'an's walls.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In spring, the first month, construction began on the northwest section of Chang'an's walls.

sentences.zh: 1冬，十月，齊悼惠王來朝，飲於太后前。

translations.literal: 1 In winter, the tenth month, the King of Qi, Daohui, came to court and drank before the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In winter, the tenth month, King Daohui of Qi came to court and drank in the Empress Dowager's presence.

sentences.zh: 帝以齊王，兄也，置之上坐。

translations.literal: The Emperor, taking the King of Qi as his elder brother, seated him in the seat of honor.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, treating the King of Qi as his elder brother, gave him the seat of honor.

sentences.zh: 太后怒，酌鴆酒置前，賜齊王為壽。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager was angry, poured poison wine and set it before him, and bestowed it on the King of Qi to wish him long life.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager was angry, poured poison wine, set it before him, and offered it to the King of Qi as a toast for long life.

sentences.zh: 齊王起，帝亦起取卮；

translations.literal: The King of Qi rose; the Emperor also rose to take the cup;
translations.idiomatic: The King of Qi rose; the Emperor rose as well to take the cup;

sentences.zh: 太后恐，自起泛帝卮。

translations.literal: the Empress Dowager was afraid and herself rose to spill the Emperor's cup.
translations.idiomatic: the Empress Dowager was alarmed and rose herself to spill the Emperor's cup.

sentences.zh: 齊王怪之，因不敢飲，佯醉去；

translations.literal: The King of Qi thought it strange and therefore dared not drink, feigned drunkenness and left;
translations.idiomatic: The King of Qi found it strange, dared not drink, feigned drunkenness, and left;

sentences.zh: 問知其鴆，大恐。

translations.literal: on inquiry learned it was poison and was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: and on inquiry learned it was poisoned—he was terrified.

sentences.zh: 齊內史士說王，使獻城陽郡為魯元公主湯沐邑。

translations.literal: The interior secretary of Qi admonished the king and had him present Chengyang commandery as Princess Yuan of Lu's fief for bathing and grooming.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's interior secretary admonished the king and had him offer Chengyang commandery as Princess Yuan of Lu's fief.

sentences.zh: 太后喜，乃罷歸齊王。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager was pleased and then dismissed him and sent the King of Qi home.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager was pleased and let the King of Qi return to Qi.

sentences.zh: ----2春，正月，癸酉，有兩龍見蘭陵家人井中。

translations.literal: ----2 In spring, the first month, on guiyou, two dragons appeared in a commoner's well at Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In spring, the first month, on guiyou, two dragons were seen in a commoner's well at Lanling.

sentences.zh: ----3隴西地震。

translations.literal: ----3 Longxi suffered an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 Longxi was shaken by an earthquake.

translations.literal: ----4 In summer there was drought.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 In summer there was drought.

sentences.zh: ----5郃陽侯仲薨。

translations.literal: ----5 Marquis of Heyang, Zhong, died.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 Marquis of Heyang Zhong died.

sentences.zh: ----6酇文終侯蕭何病，上親自臨視，因問曰：「君即百歲後，誰可代君者？

translations.literal: ----6 Marquis of Pei, Wenzhong, Xiao He was ill; the Emperor personally went to visit him and asked, saying, “When you reach a hundred years, who can replace you?
translations.idiomatic: ----6 Marquis of Pei Wenzhong Xiao He fell ill; the Emperor visited him in person and asked, “When you are gone, who can replace you?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「知臣莫如主。

translations.literal: ” He replied, saying, “No one knows a minister like his lord.
translations.idiomatic: ” He replied, “No one knows a minister like his lord.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「曹參何如？

translations.literal: ” The Emperor said, “How about Cao Shen?
translations.idiomatic: ” The Emperor said, “What of Cao Shen?

sentences.zh: 」何頓首曰：「帝得之矣，臣死不恨！

translations.literal: ” He kowtowed and said, “Your Majesty has got the right man; I die without regret!
translations.idiomatic: ” He kowtowed and said, “Your Majesty has the right man; I die without regret!

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，辛未，何薨。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on xinwei, He died.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on xinwei, Xiao He died.

sentences.zh: 何置田宅，必居窮僻處，為家，不治垣屋。

translations.literal: When He set up fields and houses he always dwelt in poor and remote places; as head of the family he did not repair walls and roofs.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao He acquired land and houses he always chose poor, remote sites; as head of the household he would not build high walls or fine roofs.

sentences.zh: 曰：「後世賢，師吾儉；

translations.literal: He said, “If later generations are worthy, take me as teacher in thrift;
translations.idiomatic: He said, “If later generations are worthy, let them learn thrift from me;

sentences.zh: 不賢，毋為勢家所奪。

translations.literal: if unworthy, let them not be seized by powerful families.
translations.idiomatic: if unworthy, let them not be seized by powerful families.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以曹參為相國。

translations.literal: On guisi, Cao Shen was made chancellor of state.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Cao Shen was appointed chancellor of state.

sentences.zh: 參聞何薨，告舍人：「趣治行！

translations.literal: When Shen heard that He had died, he told his retainers, “Hurry and pack for the journey!
translations.idiomatic: When Shen heard Xiao He had died, he told his retainers, “Pack at once for the journey!

sentences.zh: 吾將入相。

translations.literal: I am about to enter the capital as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: I am about to become chancellor.

sentences.zh: 」居無何，使者果召參。

translations.literal: ” Before long an envoy indeed summoned Shen.
translations.idiomatic: ” Before long an envoy did summon Shen.

sentences.zh: 始，參微時，與蕭何善；

translations.literal: At first, when Shen was in humble circumstances, he and Xiao He were on good terms;
translations.idiomatic: Early on, when Shen was still obscure, he and Xiao He were close;

sentences.zh: 及為將相，有隙；

translations.literal: when they became general and chancellor there was a rift;
translations.idiomatic: when they became general and chancellor they fell out;

sentences.zh: 至何且死，所推賢唯參。

translations.literal: but when He was about to die, the worthy man he recommended was only Shen.
translations.idiomatic: yet when Xiao He was dying, the worthy man he recommended was Shen alone.

sentences.zh: 參代何為相，舉事無所變更，一遵何約束：擇郡國吏木訥於文辭、重厚長者，即召除為丞相史；

translations.literal: Shen replaced He as chancellor; in all affairs he made no changes and followed He's regulations entirely: he chose commandery and state clerks who were wooden and slow in literary phrasing, men of weight and long standing, and at once summoned and appointed them as the chancellor's clerks;
translations.idiomatic: Shen succeeded Xiao He as chancellor; he changed nothing and followed Xiao He's rules entirely: he chose commandery and state officials who were plain and awkward in rhetoric, men of substance and long experience, and at once summoned them to be the chancellor's clerks;

sentences.zh: 吏之言文刻深、欲務聲名者，輒斥去之。

translations.literal: clerks whose words were literary, harsh, and deep, who wished to pursue reputation, he at once dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: officials who spoke in sharp, ornate prose and sought fame he promptly dismissed.

sentences.zh: 日夜飲醇酒。

translations.literal: Day and night he drank strong wine.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night he drank strong wine.

sentences.zh: 卿、大夫以下吏及賓客見參不事事，來者皆欲有言，參輒飲以醇酒；

translations.literal: When clerks, grandees, and subordinate officials and guests saw that Shen did not attend to affairs and came wishing to speak, Shen would at once ply them with strong wine;
translations.idiomatic: When ministers, grandees, subordinate officials, and guests saw that Shen attended to nothing and came wishing to speak, he at once plied them with strong wine;

sentences.zh: 間欲有所言，復飲之，醉而後去，終莫得開說，以為常。

translations.literal: if in the interval they wished to say something, he would drink them again; when drunk they would leave—in the end none could open their case, and this became the norm.
translations.idiomatic: if they still wished to speak, he would ply them again; they left drunk and never got to make their point—this became routine.

sentences.zh: 見人有細過，專掩匿覆蓋之，府中無事。

translations.literal: When he saw men with small faults he would specially conceal and cover them; in the office there was no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw minor faults he would cover them up; the chancellor's office was untroubled.

sentences.zh: 參子窋為中大夫。

translations.literal: Shen's son Zhu was a palace grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Shen's son Zhu was a palace grandee.

sentences.zh: 帝怪相國不治事，以為「豈少朕與？

translations.literal: The Emperor wondered that the chancellor of state did not govern affairs and thought, “Does he think me too young?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wondered that the chancellor neglected affairs and thought, “Does he think I am too young?

sentences.zh: 」使窋歸，以其私問參。

translations.literal: ” He sent Zhu home to question Shen privately.
translations.idiomatic: ” He sent Zhu home to question Shen privately.

sentences.zh: 參怒，笞窋二百，曰：「趣入侍！

translations.literal: Shen was angry and flogged Zhu two hundred strokes, saying, “Hurry back to attend at court!
translations.idiomatic: Shen was furious and flogged Zhu two hundred strokes, saying, “Get back to court at once!

sentences.zh: 天下事非若所當言也！

translations.literal: Affairs of All under Heaven are not what you ought to speak of!
translations.idiomatic: Affairs of the realm are not for you to discuss!

sentences.zh: 」至朝時，帝讓參曰：「乃者我使諫君也。

translations.literal: ” When he came to court the Emperor reproached Shen, saying, “Just now I had you admonish your father.
translations.idiomatic: ” At court the Emperor reproached Shen: “Just now I had you admonish your father.

sentences.zh: 」參免冠謝曰：「陛下自察聖武孰與高帝？

translations.literal: ” Shen removed his cap and apologized, saying, “Your Majesty, consider for yourself—whose sagely martial prowess compares with the High Emperor's?
translations.idiomatic: ” Shen removed his cap and apologized: “Your Majesty, consider—whose sagely prowess compares with the High Emperor's?

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「朕乃安敢望先帝！

translations.literal: ” The Emperor said, “How would I dare look to the late Emperor!
translations.idiomatic: ” The Emperor said, “How would I dare compare myself to the late Emperor!

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「陛下觀臣能孰與蕭何賢？

translations.literal: ” He said again, “Your Majesty, consider—whose ability compares with Xiao He's worth?
translations.idiomatic: ” He said again, “Your Majesty, consider—whose ability compares with Xiao He's?

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「君似不及也。

translations.literal: ” The Emperor said, “You seem not to reach him.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Emperor said, “You seem not to match him.

sentences.zh: 」參曰：「陛下言之是也。

translations.literal: ” Shen said, “Your Majesty speaks rightly.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shen said, “Your Majesty speaks rightly.

sentences.zh: 高帝與蕭何定天下，法令既明。

translations.literal: The High Emperor and Xiao He settled All under Heaven; the laws and orders are already clear.
translations.idiomatic: The High Emperor and Xiao He settled the realm; the laws are already clear.

sentences.zh: 今陛下垂拱，參等守職，遵而勿失，不亦可乎？

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty sits with hands folded; Shen and others keep their posts, hold fast and do not lose them—is that not acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty reigns at ease; Shen and the rest keep their posts and hold to what was established without loss—is that not enough?

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「善！

translations.literal: ” The Emperor said, “Good!
translations.idiomatic: ” The Emperor said, “Good!

sentences.zh: 參為相國，出入三年，百姓歌之曰：「蕭何為法，較若畫一；

translations.literal: Shen served as chancellor of state, coming and going for three years; the people sang of him, saying, “Xiao He made the law, uniform as if drawn with one stroke;
translations.idiomatic: Shen served as chancellor for three years; the people sang: “Xiao He made the laws, uniform as if drawn with one stroke;

sentences.zh: 曹參代之，守而勿失。

translations.literal: Cao Shen replaced him and kept them without loss.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shen replaced him and kept them without loss.

sentences.zh: 載其清淨，民以寧壹。

translations.literal: He carried on that purity and quiet; the people were thereby settled as one.
translations.idiomatic: He carried on that quiet rule; the people were at peace.

sentences.zh: 」----1春，發長安六百里內男女十四萬六千人城長安，三十日罷。

translations.literal: ” ----1 In spring, within six hundred li of Chang'an, one hundred forty-six thousand men and women were mobilized to wall Chang'an; after thirty days they were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: ” ----1 In spring, one hundred forty-six thousand men and women within six hundred li of Chang'an were mobilized to wall the city; after thirty days they were dismissed.

sentences.zh: ----2以宗室女為公主，嫁匈奴冒頓單于。

translations.literal: ----2 A daughter of the imperial clan was made a princess and married to Maodun, chanyu of the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 An imperial clanswoman was made a princess and married to Maodun, chanyu of the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 是時，冒頓方強，為書，使使遺高后，辭極褻嫚。

translations.literal: At that time Maodun was just then strong; he wrote a letter and sent an envoy to present it to Empress Gao; the wording was extremely lewd and insulting.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Maodun was at the height of his power; he wrote a letter and sent an envoy to Empress Gao with wording that was grossly lewd and insulting.

sentences.zh: 高后大怒，召將相大臣，議斬其使者，發兵擊之。

translations.literal: Empress Gao was greatly angered, summoned generals, chancellors, and great ministers, and discussed beheading his envoy and sending troops to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Gao was furious, summoned generals, chancellors, and ministers, and debated executing the envoy and sending troops to attack.

sentences.zh: 樊噲曰：「臣願得十萬眾橫行匈奴中！

translations.literal: Fan Kuai said, “Your servant wishes to have one hundred thousand men and march at will through the Xiongnu!
translations.idiomatic: Fan Kuai said, “Give me one hundred thousand men and I will march at will through the Xiongnu!

sentences.zh: 」中郎將季布曰：「噲可斬也！

translations.literal: ” Palace gentleman-general Ji Bu said, “Kuai should be beheaded!
translations.idiomatic: ” Palace gentleman-general Ji Bu said, “Kuai deserves execution!

sentences.zh: 前匈奴圍高帝於平城，漢兵三十二萬，噲為上將軍，不能解圍。

translations.literal: Formerly the Xiongnu besieged the High Emperor at Pingcheng; Han had three hundred twenty thousand troops and Kuai was supreme general, yet could not break the siege.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xiongnu besieged the High Emperor at Pingcheng, Han had three hundred twenty thousand troops and Kuai was supreme general, yet could not break the siege.

sentences.zh: 今歌吟之聲未絕，傷夷者甫起，而噲欲搖動天下，妄言以十萬眾橫行，是面謾也。

translations.literal: Now the sound of songs has not yet ceased and the wounded have just risen, yet Kuai wishes to shake All under Heaven and rashly speaks of marching at will with one hundred thousand—this is lying to one's face.
translations.idiomatic: The songs of victory have barely ended and the wounded have just risen, yet Kuai would shake the realm and boast of marching at will with one hundred thousand—this is bare-faced deceit.

sentences.zh: 且夷狄譬如禽獸，得其善言不足喜，惡言不足怒也。

translations.literal: Moreover the barbarians are like birds and beasts: receiving their fine words is not worth joy, nor their evil words worth anger.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover barbarians are like birds and beasts: fine words are not worth rejoicing over, nor foul words worth anger.

sentences.zh: 」高后曰：「善！

translations.literal: ” Empress Gao said, “Good!
translations.idiomatic: ” Empress Gao said, “Good!

sentences.zh: 」令大謁者張釋報書，深自謙遜以謝之，並遺以車二乘，馬二駟。

translations.literal: ” She ordered Grand Usher Zhang Shi to reply to the letter, deeply humble himself in apology, and also send as gifts two carriages and two teams of four horses.
translations.idiomatic: ” She ordered Grand Usher Zhang Shi to reply with a deeply humble apology and also send two carriages and two teams of four horses as gifts.

sentences.zh: 冒頓復使使來謝，曰：「未嘗聞中國禮義，陛下幸而赦之。

translations.literal: Maodun again sent an envoy to apologize, saying, “I have never heard of the rites and righteousness of China; Your Majesty was gracious and pardoned me.
translations.idiomatic: Maodun sent another envoy to apologize: “I had never heard of China's rites and righteousness; Your Majesty was gracious to pardon me.

sentences.zh: 」因獻馬，遂和親。

translations.literal: ” He then presented horses, and thereupon they made a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: ” He presented horses, and peace through marriage followed.

sentences.zh: ----3夏，五月，立閩越君搖為東海王。

translations.literal: ----3 In summer, the fifth month, the Lord of Minyue, Yao, was established as King of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In summer, the fifth month, Lord Yao of Minyue was made King of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 搖與無諸，皆越王句踐之後也，從諸侯滅秦，功多，其民便附，故立之。

translations.literal: Yao and Wuzhu were both descendants of King Goujian of Yue; they followed the feudal lords in destroying Qin, their merit was great, and their people were readily attached—therefore they were established.
translations.idiomatic: Yao and Wuzhu were both descendants of King Goujian of Yue; they followed the lords in destroying Qin with great merit, and their people were readily loyal—therefore they were enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 都東甌，世號東甌王。

translations.literal: He made his capital at Dong'ou and for generations was called King of Dong'ou.
translations.idiomatic: His capital was at Dong'ou; for generations he was called King of Dong'ou.

sentences.zh: ----4六月，發諸侯王、列侯徒隸二萬人城長安。

translations.literal: ----4 In the sixth month, twenty thousand convict laborers of feudal kings and marquises were mobilized to wall Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 In the sixth month, twenty thousand convict laborers of feudal kings and marquises were mobilized to wall Chang'an.

sentences.zh: ----5秋，七月，都廄災。

translations.literal: ----5 In autumn, the seventh month, the imperial stables burned.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 In autumn, the seventh month, the imperial stables burned.

sentences.zh: ----6是歲，蜀湔氐反，擊平之。

translations.literal: ----6 That year the Qian Di of Shu Jian rebelled and were struck down and pacified.

sentences.zh: 1冬，十月，立皇后張氏。

sentences.zh: 奉常叔孫通諫曰：「此高帝月出遊衣冠之道也，子孫奈何乘宗廟道上行哉！

translations.literal: ” Tong said, “The Son of Heaven has no mistaken actions.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shusun Tong said, “A ruler makes no mistaken actions.

sentences.zh: 今已作，百姓皆知之矣。

sentences.zh: 」上乃詔有司立原廟。

sentences.zh: ::臣光曰：過者，人之所必不免也，惟聖賢為能知而改之。

translations.literal: :: Your servant Guang says: To err is what no person can avoid; only the sage and worthy can know it and amend it.
translations.idiomatic: :: Your servant Guang says: Faults are what no one can avoid; only the sage and worthy can recognize them and correct them.

sentences.zh: 古之聖王，患其有過而不自知也，故設誹謗之木，置敢諫之鼓，豈畏百姓之聞其過哉！

translations.literal: The sage kings of old, fearing that they had faults yet did not know them, therefore set up the timber for slander and placed the drum for bold remonstrance—how could they have feared the common people hearing their faults!
translations.idiomatic: The sage kings of old, fearing they might err yet not know it, set up the timber for slander and placed the drum for bold remonstrance—were they afraid of the people hearing their faults!

sentences.zh: 是以仲虺美成湯曰：「改過不吝。

translations.literal: Therefore Zhong Hui praised Cheng Tang, saying, “To amend faults without regret.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Zhong Hui praised Cheng Tang, saying, “To amend faults without regret.

sentences.zh: 」傅說戒高宗曰：「無恥過作非。

translations.literal: ” Fuyue admonished Gaozong, saying, “Be not ashamed of faults and doing wrong.
translations.idiomatic: ” Fuyue admonished Gaozong, saying, “Be not ashamed of faults and doing wrong.

sentences.zh: 」由是觀之，則為人君者，固不以無過為賢，而以改過為美也。

translations.literal: ” From this we see that for one who is ruler, it is surely not to have no faults that counts as worthy, but to amend faults that counts as beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: ” From this we see that for a ruler it is surely not to be without fault that is admirable, but to amend faults that is praiseworthy.

sentences.zh: 今叔孫通諫孝惠，乃雲「人主無過舉」，是教人君以文過遂非也，豈不繆哉！

translations.literal: Now when Shusun Tong remonstrated with Emperor Hui, he yet said, “The Son of Heaven has no mistaken actions”—this teaches rulers to gloss over faults and persist in error; is it not absurd!
translations.idiomatic: Now when Shusun Tong remonstrated with Emperor Hui he said, “A ruler makes no mistaken actions”—this teaches rulers to gloss over faults and persist in error; is that not absurd!
